pt.tomo_sec33_risk_cards_intro: The following cards detail the five primary individual risks with the highest economic impact on business continuity:

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Single-phase power feed from a single panel without 2N redundancy.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Immediate shutdown of auxiliary electronics and management plane outage.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Point-to-point 10Gb DCI link between sites without redundant ring topology.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Write lock on transactional virtual machines and storage split-brain.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Compressor failure on uncontained high-density perimeter cooling unit.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Thermal server trip within 18 minutes due to hot-air recirculation.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing Tier-0 PAM bastion and brittle directory synchronization across entities.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Identity plane freeze and plant-level ERP authentication lockout.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing WORM immutability and lack of an isolated Cyber Recovery Vault.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Irreversible backup encryption or purge during enterprise ransomware outbreak.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Fibre Channel I/O paths without active multipathing across controllers.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Transactional storage freeze during firmware maintenance reboots.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: IPSec tunnels over commodity internet without dynamic SD-WAN failover.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Telemetry loss to operational dispatch systems stalling industrial product dispatch.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Core database instances without synchronous high-availability cross-site replicas.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Potential data loss and manual recovery with RTO exceeding 8 hours.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing mandatory cost-center tagging policies across public cloud tenants.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Undetected budget drift and recurring licensing overlap.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: End-of-life hardware and unsupported operating systems operating near failure.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Total plant scale shutdown with direct downtime losses of impacto operacional significativo.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Disruption of Core Transactional Processing Platforms
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Dispatch PC operating in single-phase non-redundant architecture.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Halted operational transaction processing at a burn rate of impacto operacional significativor.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Deployment of redundant industrial IPC ring with scale hardware bypass.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Excessive Recovery Time from Physical Tape Restores
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Restore procedures depend on physical transport of LTO magnetic tapes.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Effective RTO exceeding 18 hours during major data corruption events.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Implementation of immutable WORM storage tier and cloud replication.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Compute Saturation & upcoming renewal cycles Contract Renewal Shock
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: RAM utilization continuously exceeding 90% and VMware EoL milestones.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Expansion deadlock and steep price escalation during license renewals.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Migration to next-generation sovereign hyperconverged platform.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Thermal Recirculation Across Primary Compute Racks
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Lack of hot/cold aisle containment in primary technical datacenter.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Accelerated CPU component aging and risk of thermal shutdown.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Installation of physical cold-aisle containment and BMS IoT sensors.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Identity Perimeter Disjointedness & NIS2 Compliance Lag
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Shared privileged administrative accounts and disjointed filiales internacionales forests.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Credential compromise risk and regulatory compliance exposure.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Identity forest consolidation, PAM deployment, and mandatory MFA.

T1.inventory: 2 technical rooms at primary headquarters, generator sets in ring topology, N+1 UPS schemes, gas fire suppression, and perimeter HVAC.
findings: Absence of hot/cold aisle aerodynamic containment causing thermal recirculation across compute racks at ASHRAE limits.
Lack of real-time IoT power telemetry on electrical panels and PDUs, preventing phase-level capacity measurement.
Absence of biometric access controls at airlocks and electronic work permits (ePtW) required for NIS2 compliance.
Lack of automated correlation between environmental sensors and fire suppression systems for adjacent containment.
Electromechanical preventive maintenance managed reactively without centralized CMMS or live-load transfer testing.
strengths: Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems in N+1 redundancy with certified preventive maintenance routines.
Precision air conditioning units (CRAC) providing environmental control across technical datacenter rooms.
Automated clean-agent fire suppression and detection deployed in primary technical spaces.
Optical and thermal fire detection zoning under raised floors and ceilings complying with engineering standards.
Monitored electrical distribution switchboards and technical alarms integrated into operations control.

T2.inventory: 3 hyperconverged nodes running legacy VMware ESXi and Windows/Linux server workloads with mixed cloud instances.
findings: Structural CPU and memory saturation (>90%) preventing N+1 failover between technical rooms without workload degradation.
Absence of a unified corporate managed Kubernetes platform with security guardrails and service mesh.
Fragmented public cloud adoption lacking automated Landing Zone governance and policy enforcement guardrails.
Absence of declarative Infrastructure as Code (IaC) pipelines for continuous provisioning and version tracking.
Absence of Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) telemetry linked to core business flows.
strengths: Centralized hyperconverged compute cluster delivering dense processing capacity for corporate workloads.
Standardized operating system base templates and container execution environments for microservices.
Production hosting of mission-critical workloads (SAP S/4HANA) on Tier-1 enterprise hyperscalers (GCP/Azure).
Automated virtual server cloning and baseline deployment procedures across primary clusters.
Hypervisor-level automated high availability (HA) failover operational across compute nodes.

T3.inventory: Dual-core switching infrastructure, perimeter firewalls, and SD-WAN links interconnecting 18 operating country sites.
findings: Access layer switches across remote quarries and industrial plants approaching commercial End-of-Life (EoL).
Secondary plant interconnects dependent on static IPSec tunnels lacking dynamic traffic steering and SD-WAN failover.
Point-to-point Data Center Interconnect (DCI) lacking physical ring topology and exterior conduit diversification.
Cloud interconnect architecture lacking centralized transit routing (Cloud Router) and automated multi-region failover.
Manual network administration via CLI without declarative NetDevOps workflows or version-controlled configurations.
strengths: Dual-core backbone switching infrastructure with redundant uplinks across technical distribution frames.
Corporate WAN and SD-WAN connectivity established across manufacturing plants, quarries, and branch offices.
Dedicated high-speed 10 Gbps point-to-point fiber interconnecting primary operational datacenters.
High-performance direct interconnect ports linking core routing to public cloud transit hubs.
Centralized bandwidth monitoring probes and active link telemetry supervised in network consoles.

T4.inventory: Enterprise SAN arrays and NAS clusters replicating asynchronously across dual technical rooms.
findings: Lack of native Calidad de Servicio (QoS) bandwidth shaping on SAN arrays, exposing critical databases to I/O noisy neighbors.
Fragmented audit logging on storage controllers without dedicated write-once-read-many (WORM) audit vaults.
Reliance on local snapshot copies without physical cyber isolation against targeted ransomware encryption campaigns.
Absence of strict WORM immutability (SnapLock) activation across mission-critical volume snapshots for NIS2 compliance.
Operational friction and blurred boundary delineation in storage administration between internal IT and external support.
subpillars: Security & Access Controls for Data Platforms
strengths: High-performance enterprise storage arrays featuring dynamic capacity allocation and thin-provisioning.
Storage capacity thresholds monitored with proactive alert notifications in central dashboards.
Scheduled snapshot policies and asynchronous block-level replication between active datacenters.
Protected enterprise storage volumes configured with accidental deletion safeguards and data-at-rest encryption.
Native SAN storage volume integration supporting corporate hypervisor clusters.

T5.inventory: Tape-based and disk backup targets with manual disaster recovery playbooks and scheduled off-site replication.
findings: Concentration of datacenter resilience within a shared geographic perimeter, creating a geographic Single Point of Failure.
Technical recovery times (RTO > 4 hours) exceeding operational tolerance thresholds for continuous core transaction processing.
Absence of scheduled, full-scale disaster recovery exercises (game days) under live production mains power disconnection.
Absence of an isolated Cyber Recovery Vault with automated forensic data validation prior to mass restore execution.
Lack of symmetric standby capacity across twin datacenters preventing transparent workload failover without shutdown.
strengths: Documented contingency and disaster recovery operational procedures for essential industrial systems.
Scheduled disk and tape backup policies with verified off-site custody procedures.
Skilled internal engineering team possessing deep operational experience in manual plant system restoration.
Air-gapped offline magnetic tape backups maintained in physically isolated custody facilities.
Local electromechanical component redundancy and automated core server service failover.

T6.inventory: Centralized Active Directory domains, endpoint EDR agents, and outsourced SOC monitoring alerts.
findings: Identity plane fragmentation and persistence of over-privileged static administrative credentials lacking dynamic JIT elevation.
Absence of an enterprise Privileged Access Management (PAM) vault enforcing automated credential rotation and session monitoring.
Infrequent security configuration baseline audits lacking automated configuration drift detection across systems.
Partial vulnerability scanning coverage omitting legacy virtual machines, industrial gateways, and acquired subsidiaries.
Flat industrial plant network topology lacking East-West microsegmentation, allowing undetected threat propagation.
strengths: Centralized enterprise identity and access management directory (Active Directory).
Enforced corporate password complexity policies and initial administrative role segregation.
Homogeneous endpoint detection and response (EDR) agent deployment with external SOC monitoring.
Scheduled external perimeter penetration scanning and corporate operating system update cycles.
Next-generation perimeter firewalls enforcing corporate network traffic filtering and secure VPN.

T7.inventory: Relational database clusters (SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL) and central ITSM ticketing platform.
findings: Misalignment between technical infrastructure SLAs and core manufacturing operations, obscuring plant-level outage impact.
Manual incident triage and dispatch workflows lacking intelligent routing based on industrial operational criticality.
Absence of an automated, federated Configuration Management Database (CMDB) maintaining live dependency maps.
Reactive root cause analysis (RCA) procedures lacking institutionalized Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) error budgets.
Fragmented monitoring tooling lacking cross-domain causal event correlation between on-premise, cloud, and OT environments.
strengths: Documented IT service catalog and service level agreements (SLAs) established for internal business units.
Centralized IT Service Management (ITSM) ticketing platform structuring operational incidents and requests.
Centralized hardware and software license inventory maintained by the IT infrastructure department.
Structured post-incident reviews conducted following major service outages to identify direct causes.
Core infrastructure telemetry probes (CPU, memory, storage, ping) transmitting alerts to central consoles.

T8.inventory: ERP applications (SAP), logistics management platforms, and multi-cloud SaaS subscriptions.
findings: Critical architectural obsolescence across legacy operating systems and database engines lacking budgeted modernization paths.
Asymmetric governance between corporate headquarters and newly acquired subsidiaries, perpetuating operational silos.
Absence of continuous, quantified technical risk governance modeled under Open FAIR standards.
Reactive cloud financial governance lacking automated resource tagging enforcement and showback/chargeback models.
Absence of executive dashboards correlating technology investments with measurable plant productivity gains.
subpillars: Value Realization, Executive Metrics & Continuous Improvement
strengths: Strategic technology roadmap aligned with corporate business growth and digital modernization goals.
Periodic IT governance committee and structured capital expenditure approval processes.
Formal corporate information security policies and accounting/tax compliance oversight.
Centralized monthly billing visibility within multi-cloud consoles (GCP, Azure, and OCI).
Consolidated IT operational expenditure metrics tracked for senior financial leadership.

T9.inventory: Managed Windows 11 and macOS corporate endpoints, Microsoft 365 productivity suite, and mobile MDM profiles.
findings: Plant and quarry endpoint devices administered locally without centralized modern device management enrollment.
Vulnerability across shared industrial plant workstations lacking passwordless biometric or FIDO2 authentication.
Document sprawl across unmanaged cloud repositories lacking automated lifecycle and data retention governance policies.
Manual endpoint provisioning and workstation support processes increasing fulfillment lead times across remote facilities.
Absence of Digital Employee Experience (DEX) real-time telemetry for proactive degradation and latency detection.
subpillars: Productividad, Colaboración y Gestión del Conocimiento
strengths: Standardized corporate endpoint fleet operating under unified modern management baselines.
Secure remote connectivity and multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled for knowledge workers.
Cloud collaboration and productivity suites (M365) widely adopted across business units.
Structured Level-1 service desk and automated operating system security patch distribution.
Direct communication channels and periodic user satisfaction surveys conducted by the IT team.

T10.inventory: Mission-critical core processing engines, enterprise clearing interfaces, and operational transactional platforms.
findings: Core transactional terminals and processing engines operating on outdated hardware configurations and legacy operating systems.
Software modifications on legacy transactional components applied manually without version control in Git repositories.
Batch processing queues and data transfers concentrated in peak operating windows causing storage controller I/O spikes.
Direct database-level point-to-point links between legacy and modern systems lacking governed API contracts.
Critical dependence on tacit operational knowledge held by specialized personnel approaching retirement on legacy stacks.
strengths: Core transactional processing engines maintained with verified operational stability and scheduled maintenance.
Robust, well-rehearsed manual dispatch continuity procedures during communication disruptions.
Automated transactional synchronization interfaces transferring event logs and clearing records to central enterprise ERP.
Functional point-to-point integration connectors guaranteeing dispatch and billing continuity.
Dedicated and highly qualified on-site operational staff ensuring resilient local execution.

pt.tomo_triad_bottleneck_desc: Operational reliance on manual interventions by internal engineering teams and facility vulnerability during network degradation.
pt.tomo_triad_gap_desc: High resource pressure across core clusters (>90%), baseline operational telemetry, and upcoming software contract renewals requiring strategic consolidation.
pt.tomo_triad_strength_desc: Robust mechanical fire suppression across technical facilities alongside centralized structured storage.

T1.operational_mission: physical data center facilities, electrical continuity, and precision climate control
T1.dilemma_anchor: When evaluating electromechanical resilience and physical facility redundancy,
T1.posture_modernization_focus: reinforcing electromechanical redundancy and precision cooling to safeguard uninterrupted power to core systems

T2.operational_mission: physical and virtual compute platforms, hypervisors, and hybrid cloud workloads
T2.dilemma_anchor: From a platform engineering and compute capacity standpoint,
T2.posture_modernization_focus: expanding cluster compute elasticity and ensuring automated workload failover without performance degradation

T3.operational_mission: enterprise networks, software-defined WAN, campus switching, and inter-site transit connectivity
T3.dilemma_anchor: When evaluating network transport topology and data communications resilience,
T3.posture_modernization_focus: embedding active path redundancy across transit links and enforcing automated software-defined traffic routing

T4.operational_mission: enterprise storage architecture, SAN/NAS arrays, persistent volume fabrics, and backup repositories
T4.dilemma_anchor: From a persistent storage architecture and data tiering perspective,
T4.posture_modernization_focus: guaranteeing storage throughput and eliminating I/O bottlenecks across mission-critical persistent volumes

T5.operational_mission: business continuity architectures, high-availability clusters, backup registries, and disaster recovery procedures
T5.dilemma_anchor: When assessing organizational survivability, disaster recovery orchestration, and cyber recovery readiness,
T5.posture_modernization_focus: tightening automated failover thresholds (RTO/RPO) and validating immutable cyber recovery procedures against systemic disruption

T6.operational_mission: cybersecurity architecture, zero trust identity governance, privileged access management, and threat defense
T6.dilemma_anchor: From an enterprise cybersecurity, perimeter defense, and identity protection standpoint,
T6.posture_modernization_focus: elevating privileged access governance, enforcing hardware-backed multi-factor authentication, and deploying continuous threat monitoring

T7.operational_mission: IT service management (ITSM), incident command, change governance, and operational support workflows
T7.dilemma_anchor: When reviewing operational service delivery, incident response cadences, and ITIL process maturity,
T7.posture_modernization_focus: streamlining incident triage automation, enforcing change management rigor, and reducing mean time to repair (MTTR)

T8.operational_mission: technology strategy, enterprise IT governance, portfolio prioritization, and cloud financial operations (FinOps)
T8.dilemma_anchor: From an enterprise technology governance, architectural review, and cloud financial optimization standpoint,
T8.posture_modernization_focus: enforcing automated cloud expenditure guardrails, optimizing unit economics, and aligning architectural roadmaps with business OKRs

T9.operational_mission: digital workplace engineering, unified endpoint management, collaboration tooling, and end-user support
T9.dilemma_anchor: When evaluating user computing environments, endpoint security posture, and workplace productivity tools,
T9.posture_modernization_focus: standardizing endpoint device configurations, enforcing device health compliance, and automating workstation provisioning

T10.operational_mission: core transactional processing engines, legacy applications, payment and settlement rails, and high-throughput clearing interfaces
T10.dilemma_anchor: When auditing core mission-critical platforms, high-throughput transaction processing, and legacy application resilience,
T10.posture_modernization_focus: modernizing legacy transactional dependencies, decoupling batch windows, and establishing resilient API integrations

DEFAULT.operational_mission: supporting essential operational capabilities with standardized architectural baselines
DEFAULT.dilemma_anchor: When reviewing baseline operational capabilities and architectural alignment,
DEFAULT.posture_modernization_focus: reinforcing operational controls and modernizing key infrastructure dependencies

pt.tomo_ch1_continuity_bullet_body: Os sistemas e serviços nas unidades operacionais apresentam dependências de links de comunicação únicos e infraestrutura próxima do fim de suporte, expondo a atividade diária a interrupções técnicas diante de incidentes locais.

pt.tomo_ch2_benchmark_methodology_body: A referência reflete a mediana empírica (P50) do setor de manufatura pesada, reconhecendo a assimetria real entre serviços de infraestrutura padronizados e a continuidade operacional em plantas industriais.

pt.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_1: • Out-of-Contract 24x7 OEM Emergency Engineering Intervention ({bucket_1_cost} — {bucket_1_pct} of emergency spend): Reactive engagement of Tier-3 Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specialists at emergency Time & Materials rates outside standard SLAs to rebuild hypervisors, storage arrays, or network switches whose standard support has lapsed.
pt.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_2: • Urgent Spot-Market Hardware Procurement and Dedicated Courier Logistics ({bucket_2_cost} — {bucket_2_pct} of emergency spend): Immediate spot-market purchase of replacement servers, controllers, drives, or switches at premium availability pricing, combined with dedicated same-day air/ground courier transport directly to affected facilities.
pt.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_3: • Specialized Database Recovery and Level-3 Forensic Triage Services ({bucket_3_cost} — {bucket_3_pct} of emergency spend): Engagement of external recovery engineers specialized in repairing corrupted transactional tables (core ERP/corporate databases), reconciling in-flight transactions interrupted by the crash, and performing forensic containment prior to production restart.
pt.tomo_ch3_exec_intro_p1: Este capítulo quantifica o impacto financeiro e os riscos operacionais da arquitetura atual sob o padrão internacional Open FAIR™. Seu objetivo é fornecer à Liderança de TI e ao Comitê Executivo uma base objetiva e economicamente sustentável sobre o custo real de operar com a infraestrutura em seu estado atual. Para tanto, o modelo identifica e prioriza os principais cenários de falha técnica com base em sua probabilidade e severidade, dimensionando tanto a perda recorrente que afeta o resultado no dia a dia quanto a exposição direta que a organização enfrentaria diante de contingências graves ou crises acumuladas.
pt.tomo_ch3_sec31_reconciliation_bridge: Para facilitar a alocação orçamentária e a priorização de investimentos pela Liderança, a tabela a seguir consolida a correlação direta entre o nível de maturidade técnica e o risco financeiro de cada domínio, detalhando a perda anual esperada (ALE), o custo de uma contingência severa isolada e a porcentagem de exposição sobre o total do portfólio:
pt.tomo_ch3_step1_heading: 3.1. Custo Estimado da Inação e Simulação de Estresse Financeiro
pt.tomo_ch3_step2_emergency_intro_bullet: 2. Extraordinary Emergency Recovery Costs ({total_emergency_cost}): When a critical system fails outside active vendor support coverage or exceeds internal recovery capacity, the enterprise must engage external emergency resources at contingency rates. This {total_emergency_cost} expenditure decomposes into three auditable operational buckets:

This encompasses halted shipments, stalled dispatch lines, idle operational labor hours, and delayed order processing and billing.

pt.tomo_ch3_step2_sub1_intro: When a severe failure strikes critical infrastructure (such as a primary virtualization cluster collapse or core storage corruption without immutable backups), the estimated mean time to rebuild the environment, restore data volumes, and verify transactional integrity reaches {outage_duration_hours}. An incident of this magnitude generates an estimated total financial impact of {total_event_loss}, divided into two distinct operational components:

pt.tomo_ch4_spof_section_title: 4.11. Consolidated Single Point of Failure (SPOF) Matrix
pt.tomo_ch3_p90_4: Em um horizonte cumulativo de 3 anos sem remediação arquitetônica, as perdas esperadas acumulam {var_3y_expected}, atingindo um valor em risco acumulado em 3 anos (VaR 3Y P90) de {var_3y_tail} sob estresse operacional contínuo.
pt.tomo_ch3_loss_composition_note: Nota metodológica sobre a composição do impacto: De acordo com a metodologia Open FAIR™, as perdas econômicas anualizadas não representam apenas custos indiretos de produtividade. Em incidentes graves, cerca de 50% da exposição se converte em saídas diretas de caixa para recuperação de emergência.
pt.tomo_ch2_summary_p1: O índice global consolidado de maturidade situa-se em {overall_maturity} sobre 5,00, posicionando a plataforma tecnológica no Nível 2 (Repetível). Este resultado reflete uma arquitetura de duas velocidades claramente diferenciadas. Por um lado, as capacidades de base corporativa — Armazenamento e Backup (3,30) e Posto de Trabalho Digital (3,10) — atingiram o Nível 3 (Definido), operando sob padrões documentados, arquiteturas centralizadas e níveis de serviço previsíveis.
pt.tomo_ch2_summary_p2: Por outro lado, os domínios que sustentam a execução industrial e transacional — Continuidade Operacional (2,10), Aplicações de Negócio (2,40) e Sistemas de Expedição (2,40) — permanecem na faixa reativa do Nível 2. Nestas áreas, a estabilidade operacional depende do esforço reativo da equipe técnica, configurações locais sem redundância automatizada e integrações ponto a ponto. Esta assimetria estrutural entre o ambiente corporativo e a planta industrial constitui o vetor principal de exposição operacional e financeira analisado no Capítulo 3.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T1: Data centers com robustez mecânica consolidada, penalizados por confinamento térmico e telemetria de energia básica.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T2: Stable core virtualization and hyperconverged platforms, constrained by high memory pressure and upcoming technological refresh milestones.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T3: Topologia WAN/SD-WAN operacional, necessitando reforçar segmentação IT/OT e dupla conectividade em pedreiras críticas.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T4: Arquitetura de armazenamento e backup centralizada e previsível, com políticas formais de retenção e replicação local.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T5: Procedimentos DRP não formalizados nas plantas, dependência de intervenções manuais e tempos de recuperação prolongados.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T6: Controles de segurança perimetral ativos, necessitando ampliar visibilidade em redes OT e implantar PAM.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T7: Gestão de bancos de dados transacionais estável, pendente padronizar automação de patches e governança ITSM.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T8: Ecossistema SAP/ERP consolidado nas finanças, penalizado por integrações satélite manuais e contratos de licença fragmentados.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T9: Ambiente de produtividade e posto digital padronizado no Microsoft 365, com governança madura na camada de escritório.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_T10: Local operations and distributed facility support with operational continuity processes reliant on manual procedures.
pt.tomo_ch2_driver_summary: Assimetria estrutural entre serviços corporativos padronizados (Nível 3) e operações de planta expostas (Nível 2).

pt.gloss_erc_high: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - High]:** High structural influence; a critical outage in this domain easily propagates cascades destabilizing connected enterprise systems.
pt.gloss_erc_medium: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Medium]:** Moderate structural influence; disruption remains contained, impacting only immediately adjacent workloads.
pt.gloss_erc_low: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Low/Isolated]:** Low structural influence; failures remain strictly isolated within this technical perimeter without holding-wide impact.
pt.gloss_mcda_crit_extreme: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Extreme]:** Assesses the level of direct dependency that key operational processes have on this domain. Core business operations depend critically on this platform, and an outage would cause immediate disruption of essential services.
pt.gloss_mcda_crit_high: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - High]:** Reflects high operational dependency, though a brief latency tolerance exists before core business continuity is disrupted.
pt.gloss_mcda_crit_medium: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Medium]:** The domain provides supportive or back-office services whose temporary downtime is manageable via standard contingency procedures.
pt.gloss_mcda_reg_critical: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Critical]:** Severe regulatory exposure under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001), where security deficiencies directly incur high statutory penalties and direct corporate liability.
pt.gloss_mcda_reg_moderate: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Moderate]:** Strict corporate compliance and security baseline mandates apply, requiring periodic independent IT control audits.
pt.gloss_mcda_reg_standard: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Standard]:** Standard operational compliance based on engineering best practices without direct statutory critical scrutiny.
pt.gloss_mcda_viab_favorable: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Feasible]:** Transformation feasibility is favorable. Modernization initiatives can be delivered with mature technologies and market resources without critical disruption.
pt.gloss_mcda_viab_complex: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Complex]:** High execution complexity due to structural technical debt, maintenance bottlenecks, or specialized skill scarcity.
pt.gloss_dii_high: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Stability]:** The extremely low Decision Instability Index mathematically certifies that findings are robust and unaffected by small evidence variations.
pt.gloss_dii_moderate: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - Moderate Stability]:** Moderate sensitivity; findings are substantially stable though specific sub-scores depend on evolving architectural interpretation.
pt.gloss_dii_volatile: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Sensitivity]:** High volatility; limited evidentiary backing suggests further confirmation is required to lock target maturity scores.

pt.tomo_ch2_sec2_intro: A maturidade é avaliada em uma escala analítica de 1,00 a 5,00 segmentada em intervalos contínuos de 0,80 pontos, onde cada nível define um patamar de controle operacional e governança:

pt.sec_3_2_detailed_diagnostics_intro: Apresenta-se a seguir a análise técnica e processual exaustiva para cada uma das capacidades avaliadas neste domínio. Cada ficha contrasta a autoavaliação inicial com as evidências empíricas de auditoria, justificando objetivamente a maturidade factual atribuída e estabelecendo a trajetória pragmática de modernização para o nível seguinte.

pt.diag_rationale_divergence_gap: A autoavaliação inicial da organização projetava uma pontuação de {dec_fmt} sobre 5,0. No entanto, a verificação técnica e as evidências forenses constatam {finding_clause}. Por isso, a auditoria calibra a maturidade operacional em {score_fmt} ({band_label}) para fundamentar de forma objetiva as prioridades de modernização no Volume 2.
pt.diag_rationale_divergence_conservative: A operação técnica observada supera a autoavaliação declarada ({dec_fmt}), calibrando-se a capacidade em {score_fmt} ({band_label}). Embora o ambiente opere com estabilidade, identifica-se {finding_clause}, definindo a margem de melhoria para os níveis seguintes.
pt.diag_rationale_divergence_aligned: A autoavaliação inicial ({dec_fmt}) e o diagnóstico técnico coincidem plenamente ao situar a capacidade em {score_fmt} ({band_label}). A base instalada dá suporte à operação diária; no entanto, a resiliência do domínio é condicionada por {finding_clause}.
pt.diag_rationale_fact_first_low: A gestão desta capacidade encontra-se num regime inicial ({score_fmt} de 5,0 - {band_label}). A operação é severamente condicionada por {finding_clause}, exigindo controlos fundacionais no Volume 2.
pt.diag_rationale_fact_first_mid: A capacidade opera com estabilidade diária num regime {band_label} ({score_fmt} de 5,0). No entanto, a escalabilidade é limitada por {finding_clause}, orientando a consolidação.
pt.diag_rationale_fact_first_high: A capacidade demonstra maturidade consolidada ({score_fmt} de 5,0 - {band_label}), sustentada em processos padronizados. Identifica-se como oportunidade {finding_clause}.

ch3_intro_by_tower.T1: The evaluation of the {tower_title} domain across {client_name} examines electromechanical resilience, physical capacity, and critical facilities stability. This chapter documents the technical diagnosis of computer rooms and processing facilities, auditing uninterrupted power continuity, environmental cooling controls, and preventative maintenance governance over core operational assets.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T2: This chapter documents the architectural assessment of compute platforms, virtualization hypervisors, and hybrid execution environments comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The diagnosis examines cluster sizing and bin-packing capacity, CPU and memory contention, and guest operating system lifecycle management against modern decoupling paradigms.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T3: This chapter analyzes communications architecture, campus networks, and wide-area interconnection links comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The audit evaluates topological resilience against transport failures, microsegmentation and perimeter controls across trust boundaries, and latency stability across corporate services and distributed operating sites.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T4: This chapter addresses the technical diagnosis of enterprise storage platforms, primary arrays, and secondary backup repositories comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation audits database performance and latency SLA compliance, immutable ransomware protection and air-gapping defenses, and storage lifecycle capacity governance.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T5: This chapter examines the operational resilience and disaster recovery posture (BC/DR) governing {tower_title} across {client_name}. The analysis contrasts technical failover and recovery procedures against business disruption tolerances, evaluating physical facility independence, core data protection, and site operational autonomy during central outages.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T6: This section presents the evaluation of the cybersecurity posture, identity governance, and infrastructure defenses comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The diagnostic audits privileged access controls (PAM), threat detection and telemetry visibility, system hardening, and compliance with enterprise security and regulatory frameworks.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T7: This chapter evaluates service delivery maturity, operational technical support, and observability workflows comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The audit examines change control discipline, configuration management database (CMDB) accuracy, incident resolution efficacy, and proactive operational event correlation.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T8: This chapter examines the fiduciary model, technological financial transparency, and strategic technology governance comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation analyzes infrastructure cost predictability and showback across business units, software licensing optimization, and technological investment alignment with organizational priorities.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T9: This chapter addresses the diagnosis of the digital workplace, collaboration solutions, and user endpoint fleets comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The analysis evaluates device fleet standardization and homogeneity, automated lifecycle staging and patching, digital employee experience (DEX), and secure endpoint access across distributed workspaces.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T10: This chapter analyzes dedicated operational platforms, activity execution systems, and field peripherals underpinning {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation audits hardware resilience at critical operating points, transactional continuity during network contingencies, and the modernization posture of core operational systems.

pt.scorecard_commentary_low: Scoring a technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_name} domain across {client_name} operates under acute operational exposure. Gaps in engineering formalization and automation are critically concentrated within {weakest_pillar_name} ({weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), constraining overall domain resilience and mandating prioritized structural remediation.
pt.scorecard_commentary_mid: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_name} domain across {client_name} sustains baseline operations through largely manual and reactive procedures. CAPITAL_INEFFICIENCY.methodology_intro: A exposição atuarial para {domain_name} é modelada via receptor Open FAIR™ de Ineficiência de Capital, capturando vazamentos de valor em infraestrutura e licenciamento.

annex_ch4_context_gamma.cloud_native: Topologia FinOps Cloud-Native (γ={gamma:.2f}): A exposição financeira decorre de desvio de computação elástica sob demanda, instâncias não otimizadas e recursos órfãos em nuvem.
annex_ch4_context_gamma.on_prem: Governança de Infraestrutura e Licenciamento por Núcleo (γ={gamma:.2f}): A ineficiência concentra-se em capacidade hiperconvergente ociosa, passivos de licença de virtualização por núcleo e depreciação física de hardware.
annex_ch4_context_gamma.hybrid: Arbitragem de Nuvem Híbrida e Borda (γ={gamma:.2f}): A fricção financeira decorre da duplicidade de custos entre nuvem e data center local, e compromissos contratuais desalinhados.

annex_ch4_context_beta.clinical: Vulnerabilidade Clínica Aguda (β={beta:.2f}): A telemetria de pacientes e UTI opera com tolerância de amortecimento quase nula, transferindo a parada imediatamente para o atendimento clínico.
annex_ch4_context_beta.synchronous: Sensibilidade de Compensação Síncrona (β={beta:.2f}): Os trilhos de pagamento operam sem margem de amortecimento, disparando rejeição instantânea de transações e multas regulatórias.
annex_ch4_context_beta.high_tempo: Exposição Operacional de Alto Ritmo (β={beta:.2f}): A disponibilidade contínua é crítica para evitar a interrupção imediata das operações de negócio e perda direta de receitas comerciais.
annex_ch4_context_beta.buffered_silo: Amortecimento Físico por Silos e Estoque (β={beta:.2f}): A expedição fabril é parcialmente blindada por estoques intermediários e turnos compensatórios, atenuando a perda financeira direta em paradas curtas.

pt.p90_callout_finops_p1: Para avaliar o limite de resiliência fiscal e operacional deste domínio, o modelo simula um cenário adverso no qual coincidem múltiplos desvios contratuais e arquiteturais: {trigger_text}.
pt.p90_callout_finops_p2: Diante de um desvio orçamentário dessa magnitude, a regularização exige renegociação de compromissos contratuais de volume e auditoria de recursos dispersos. Sob a governança atual, estabilizar os custos exigiria uma janela de até {p90_rec_hours_str} meses.
pt.p90_callout_finops_p3: A exposição financeira total deste cenário atinge {p90_contingency_str}, dividida em: {direct_stoppage_str} em desvio de consumo sob demanda e {secondary_spend_str} em ajustes extraordinários de licenciamento e consultoria FinOps.
pt.ch4_tier1_focus_capital_inefficiency: Imminent software license true-up liabilities, contract renewals, and cumulative on-demand cloud budget drift.
pt.ch4_tier2_focus_capital_inefficiency: Oversized compute allocations, orphaned cloud resources, and lack of business unit cost allocation (showback).
pt.ch4_tier3_focus_capital_inefficiency: Decentralized SaaS sprawl and micro-subscription billing inefficiencies.
pt.ch4_tier1_focus_regulatory_and_breach: Critical exploitable vulnerabilities, lack of IT/OT segmentation, and major regulatory penalty exposure.
pt.ch4_tier2_focus_regulatory_and_breach: Gaps in continuous security monitoring (SIEM/SOC), privileged access management (PAM), and incident response.
pt.ch4_tier3_focus_regulatory_and_breach: Procedural compliance gaps and minor documentation drift without direct technical exploitability.
pt.ch4_tier1_focus_productivity_toil: Operational bottlenecks and tool failures that halt service delivery or broadly disrupt end users.
pt.ch4_tier2_focus_productivity_toil: Repetitive manual support toil, inefficient triage workflows, and absence of automated remediation.
pt.ch4_tier3_focus_productivity_toil: Self-service friction and localized fulfillment delays on non-critical tickets.
pt.ch4_tier1_focus_availability_outage: Structural single points of failure capable of halting essential operations or business continuity.
pt.ch4_tier2_focus_availability_outage: Operational vulnerabilities or incomplete redundancies that degrade performance and extend recovery duration (MTTR).
pt.ch4_tier3_focus_availability_outage: Localized non-redundant component failures with bounded operational impact.
pt.p90_callout_plant_p2: In an operational contingency of this scale across dispatch and logistics facilities, local teams transition after 30 to 60 minutes of outage to manual workaround procedures (paper waybills and decentralized weighbridge capture). While this prevents absolute transportation paralysis, it throttles throughput to 35%-45% of nominal capacity, causing transport queues, reconciliation toil, and inventory discrepancy risks. Restoring transactional sync with the corporate ERP and completing audit balancing requires a window of up to {p90_rec_hours_str} hours.

fr.nexus_rule_4_rationale: Security telemetry and anomaly detection must be seamlessly integrated into 24/7 incident management and ITSM workflows.
fr.nexus_rule_4_delay: Blind incident detection windows and lack of forensic traceability during operational disruptions.

fr.gloss_mcda_crit_extrema: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Extreme]:** Assesses the level of direct dependency that key operational processes have on this domain. Core business operations depend critically on this platform, and an outage would cause immediate disruption of essential services.
fr.gloss_mcda_crit_alta: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - High]:** Reflects high operational dependency, though a brief latency tolerance exists before core business continuity is disrupted.
fr.gloss_mcda_crit_media: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Medium]:** The domain provides supportive or back-office services whose temporary downtime is manageable via standard contingency procedures.
fr.gloss_mcda_reg_critica: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Critical]:** Severe regulatory exposure under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001), where security deficiencies directly incur high statutory penalties and direct corporate liability.
fr.gloss_mcda_reg_moderada: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Moderate]:** Strict corporate compliance and security baseline mandates apply, requiring periodic independent IT control audits.
fr.gloss_mcda_reg_estandar: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Standard]:** Standard operational compliance based on engineering best practices without direct statutory critical scrutiny.
fr.gloss_mcda_viab_fav: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Feasible]:** Transformation feasibility is favorable. Modernization initiatives can be delivered with mature technologies and market resources without critical disruption.
fr.gloss_mcda_viab_comp: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Complex]:** High execution complexity due to structural technical debt, maintenance bottlenecks, or specialized skill scarcity.
fr.gloss_dii_alta: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Stability]:** The extremely low Decision Instability Index mathematically certifies that findings are robust and unaffected by small evidence variations.
fr.gloss_dii_mod: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - Moderate Stability]:** Moderate sensitivity; findings are substantially stable though specific sub-scores depend on evolving architectural interpretation.
fr.gloss_dii_vol: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Sensitivity]:** High volatility; limited evidentiary backing suggests further confirmation is required to lock target maturity scores.
fr.gloss_erc_alta: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - High]:** High structural influence; a critical outage in this domain easily propagates cascades destabilizing connected enterprise systems.
fr.gloss_erc_media: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Medium]:** Moderate structural influence; disruption remains contained, impacting only immediately adjacent workloads.
fr.gloss_erc_baja: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Low/Isolated]:** Low structural influence; failures remain strictly isolated within this technical perimeter without holding-wide impact.
fr.gloss_spof_crit: **Single Point of Failure (SPOF) [YES - Critical]:** This domain represents an unmitigated structural bottleneck without sufficient failover, requiring immediate remediation.
fr.gloss_spof_stable: **Single Point of Failure (SPOF) [NO - Stable]:** This domain does not act as an isolated single point of failure within the overall operational topology.

fr.value_hexagon_intro: Pour fournir une perspective métier globale justifiant la modernisation, ce diagnostic complète Open FAIR par les cadres internationaux **TBM (Technology Business Management)** et **FinOps** selon six leviers de valeur :
value_hexagon_bullets: Levier 1 - Récupération du Capital Travail (Lean IT) : Coûts salariaux perdus sur des tâches manuelles automatisables.
Levier 2 - Coût d'Opportunité des Talents : Manque à gagner d'ingénieurs seniors bloqués sur la maintenance réactive.
Levier 3 - Coût du Retard des Projets : Pertes indirectes liées aux délais d'attente d'approvisionnement manuel.
Levier 4 - Élimination du Gaspillage d'Infrastructure : Surcoûts liés au surdimensionnement préventif.
Levier 5 - Évitement des Coûts de Support Étendu : Surcoûts de maintenance constructeur sur matériel obsolète.
Levier 6 - Protection contre les Risques Extrêmes : Réduction des pannes majeures et sanctions NIS2.

Plage Probabiliste : Le spectre statistique des pertes possibles jusqu'au maximum théorique.

fr.maturity_scale_intro: La maturité est mesurée sur une échelle analytique de 1,00 à 5,00, où chaque niveau correspond à un stade de contrôle :
maturity_scale_levels: **Level 1 - Initial (1.00 - 1.59):** Ad-hoc, reactive practices dependent on heroic individual efforts.
**Level 2 - Managed (1.60 - 2.59):** Basic operational processes established at tactical level with inter-silo inconsistencies.
**Level 3 - Defined (2.60 - 3.59):** Formalized and consistently documented processes across the entire enterprise.
**Level 4 - Quantitatively Managed (3.60 - 4.59):** Quantitatively measured capabilities aligned with corporate IT governance.
**Level 5 - Optimized (4.60 - 5.00):** Operational excellence model characterized by high automation and continuous improvement.

fr.systemic_resilience_intro: Pour mesurer la résilience transversale de la plateforme, le moteur calcule les indicateurs décisionnels avancés suivants à l'aide de modèles multicritères et de propagation en réseau :
systemic_resilience_indicators_list: 1. **Criticité Métier (MCDA) [Plage 0% à 100%] :** Une valeur supérieure à 80% indique un domaine supportant directement un service essentiel critique.
2. **Pression Réglementaire (MCDA) [Plage 0% à 100%] :** Une valeur supérieure à 80% indique une conformité stricte obligatoire (NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001).
3. **Faisabilité Opérationnelle (MCDA) [Plage 0% à 100%] :** Mesure la facilité technique et humaine de mise en œuvre des initiatives proposées.
4. **Indice d'Instabilité du Diagnostic (DII) [Plage 0% à 100%] :** Quantifie la robustesse mathématique du diagnostic face aux variations de preuves.
5. **Centralité de Propagation des Défaillances (ERC) [Plage 0,000 à 1,000] :** Algorithme de centralité mesurant l'effet de contagion technique en réseau.
6. **Point Unique de Défaillance (SPOF) [OUI / NON] :** Alerte sur l'absence de redondance active pour des composants d'infrastructure critiques.

fr.appendix_fair_rationale_p: Les matrices de risque qualitatives traditionnelles (Élevé/Moyen/Faible) manquent de la précision actuarielle nécessaire pour justifier les investissements. Ce diagnostic adopte la norme Open FAIR™ (ISO/IEC 27005) pour modéliser l'exposition financière annuelle.
fr.appendix_fair_dual_layer_p: Pour comprendre la propagation d'une défaillance technique jusqu'au bilan financier, l'évaluation reconstitue la chronologie de l'incident en deux couches distinctes :
fr.appendix_fair_dual_layer_b1: Couche 1 : Modélisation des Vulnérabilités (Norme FAIR-CAM™) - Étalonnage stochastique de l'efficacité défensive via courbes log-normales pour les pertes primaires.
fr.appendix_fair_dual_layer_b2: Couche 2 : Exposition Secondaire et Diligence Raisonnable (Norme FAIR-MAM™) - Simulation des pertes secondaires catastrophiques (sanctions {reg_name} jusqu'à {reg_fine_limit}) selon une courbe logistique.
fr.appendix_fair_sim_kernel_p: Le moteur de risque exécute une **simulation de Monte-Carlo de 10 000 itérations** pilotée par un processus de risque collectif composé à deux étapes (normes Bâle III) :
appendix_fair_sim_bullets: Élicitation d'Experts (Consensus Adversarial Multi-Agents) : Mise à jour bayésienne calibrant les distributions a priori.
Fréquence des Menaces (Distribution Binomiale Négative) : Modélise la sur-dispersion et les attaques en rafale.
Interception des Contrôles (Processus Binomial) : Détermine si les défenses contiennent ou cèdent face aux menaces.
Sévérité des Pertes (Distribution Log-normale Troncated) : Modélise les pertes extrêmes avec plafonnement légal.
Corrélation Multivariée (Copule Gaussienne) : Lie causalement pertes primaires et sanctions secondaires.
fr.appendix_fair_metrics_intro: En intégrant les 10 000 itérations de simulation, le moteur génère la distribution cumulée des pertes et trois métriques décisionnelles :
appendix_fair_metrics_bullets: Perte Annuelle Estimée (ALE) : La moyenne arithmétique de tous les scénarios de perte, mesurant le coût de l'inaction.
Déficit Attendu (CVaR / Expected Shortfall) : La moyenne des 2,5 % des pires pertes extrêmes.
Fourchette de Perte Plausible (Intervalle P10 - P90) : La fenêtre de volatilité opérationnelle pour la planification budgétaire.
fr.appendix_c_custody_p1: Afin de garantir l'immutabilité et la traçabilité forensique requises lors des audits d'infrastructures critiques, ce document certifie que toutes les données respectent une chaîne de conservation stricte :
fr.matrix_dim_1_path_a:
• Annualized cost of inaction estimated at **{currency}{formatted_ale_item}**/year (ALE from operational friction and unplanned downtime).
• Latent exposure in a severe crisis or cascading outage scenario reaching up to **{currency}{formatted_p90}** (P90).
• Cumulative technical debt growth and continuous rise in maintenance overhead over a 3- to 5-year horizon.
fr.matrix_dim_1_path_b:
• Progressive amortization of structural technical debt through targeted investment.
• Over **80%** reduction in systemic risk exposure and elimination of single points of failure.
• Defensible ROI grounded in eliminated downtime and reduced manual toil.
fr.matrix_dim_2_path_a:
• Reactive siloed operations heavily dependent on manual firefighting.
• Escalating Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) and reliance on emergency triage.
• Late incident detection reported by end users or business operations.
fr.matrix_dim_2_path_b:
• Unified real-time telemetry with proactive incident prevention prior to service impact.
• Radical MTTR reduction through automated procedures and executable runbooks.
• Service Level Agreements (SLAs) guaranteed by continuous observability.
fr.matrix_dim_3_path_a:
• Structural difficulty demonstrating continuous compliance during internal and external audits.
• Exposure to non-compliance findings and operational contingencies under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, ISO 27001, ISO 22301).
fr.matrix_dim_3_path_b:
• Auditable compliance by design through structured technical governance.
• Minimized non-compliance exposure and automated documentation traceability.
fr.matrix_dim_4_path_a:
• Continuous cognitive overload on IT specialists handling low-value manual toil.
• Engineering fatigue, risk of critical operational knowledge loss, and delayed strategic projects.
fr.matrix_dim_4_path_b:
• Standardization and automation of repetitive tasks, liberating engineering capacity.
• Refocusing technical talent on innovation, business scalability, and strategic growth.

methodology_three_phases_bullets: **Phase 1: Evidence Ingestion & Operational Verification:** On-site technical inspection, engineering interviews, and network/facility topology validation.
**Phase 2: Topological Dependency Modeling & SPOF Analysis:** Cascading failure propagation analysis mapping facility disruptions to core organizational operations.
**Phase 3: Quantitative Actuarial Simulation (Open FAIR):** 10,000-run Monte Carlo stochastic modeling quantifying annualized financial loss exposure (ALE) and P90 tail risk.
fr.cross_cutting_debt_title: Cross-Cutting Technical Debt Analysis & Structural Risk Patterns
fr.cross_cutting_debt_intro: Beyond vertical pillar baselines, the assessment identifies three horizontal friction patterns spanning the entire infrastructure:
fr.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_1: **1. Absence de Télémétrie Continue et Capacité Non Monitorée:** La gestion des capacités électriques et thermiques manque de surveillance télémétrique numérique en temps réel sur les tableaux généraux et bandeaux de baies (iPDU).
fr.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_2: **2. Operational Silos Between Facilities (BMS) and Central Enterprise IT Observability:** Electromechanical infrastructure operates decoupled from corporate monitoring. Environmental anomalies fail to trigger correlated early warnings, causing degradations to be discovered only after server cluster outages.
fr.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_3: **3. Procédures de Contrôle et Permis de Travail Non Structurés:** Les rondes de maintenance préventive, les tests de commutation et le contrôle d'accès des prestataires manquent de flux formels d'autorisation numérique et de traçabilité immuable.
fr.rore_value_hexagon_title: The Return on Resilience & Efficiency Hexagon (RoRE / TBM & FinOps)
fr.rore_value_hexagon_intro: Infrastructure risk mitigation unlocks direct economic value structured across six strategic levers under the TBM and FinOps frameworks:
rore_value_hexagon_bullets: **1. Labor Capital Recovery (Lean IT):** Eliminating reactive manual rounds and physical clamp measurements, freeing engineering capacity for core innovation initiatives.
**2. Cost of Delay Reduction:** Accelerating capacity provisioning and facilitating seamless post-merger technology onboarding for organizational acquisitions (M&A).

**3. Capacity Optimization & Operational Efficiency:** Eliminating throughput bottlenecks, over-provisioning, and resource waste, reducing operational platform overhead and infrastructure energy consumption by up to 28%.
**4. Extended Support Cost Avoidance:** Phasing out end-of-life (EoL) infrastructure before facing punitive non-warranty vendor maintenance pricing tiers.
**5. Tail-Risk Balance Sheet Mitigation (CVaR):** Insulating operational cash flows against catastrophic multi-day outages threatening commercial revenue and continuous operations.

**6. Regulatory & Governance Compliance Assurance:** Continuous audit-grade telemetry and incident records ensuring alignment with international resilience frameworks and preventing punitive regulatory sanctions.

ch3_intro_archetypes.INFRASTRUCTURE_PHYSICAL: This chapter presents the technical assessment of physical facilities, electromechanical power distribution, and plant networking across {tower_name} at {client_name}. The analysis evaluates infrastructure resilience across three dimensions: power and precision cooling redundancy, single point of failure (SPOF) elimination, and preventive maintenance discipline.
ch3_intro_archetypes.COMPUTE_PLATFORMS: This chapter documents the technical diagnostic of compute platforms, virtualization clusters, and workload execution environments comprising {tower_name} at {client_name}. The assessment examines cluster capacity to sustain continuous transaction throughput, hypervisor memory saturation, and operating system support lifecycles.
ch3_intro_archetypes.SECURITY_GOVERNANCE: This section presents the technical evaluation of persistence mechanisms, access controls, and operational governance across {tower_name} at {client_name}. The analysis verifies data immutability, infrastructure defense resilience, and contingency recovery readiness safeguarding enterprise continuity.

fr.ch3_intro_p1: This chapter executes the technical diagnostic of the technology platform at {client_name}, evaluating the {tower_name} infrastructure across three analytical dimensions: (1) architectural resilience against single points of failure (SPOFs) and redundancy deficits; (2) physical and logical obsolescence relative to vendor support lifecycles; and (3) the maturity of operational runbooks and preventive maintenance regimes. Triangulating these factors under the CMMI framework establishes the operational risk baseline and substantiates modernization priorities.

fr.ch4_methodological_intro: This technical diagnostic applies The Open Group international O-FAIR (Factor Analysis of Information Risk) standard to model, quantify, and prioritize infrastructure risk exposure in real financial terms. To avoid the "Flaw of Averages" (where fixed single-point estimates distort true risk), the platform engine executes a 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo actuarial simulation algorithm for every detected finding.

ch4_sec1_domain_context.INFRASTRUCTURE_PHYSICAL: Within {tower_name}, an unplanned electrical or cooling failure directly halts server rooms and network gear at primary facilities of {client_name}. ch4_sec1_domain_context.COMPUTE_PLATFORMS: Within {tower_name}, a critical compute cluster outage or hypervisor lock simultaneously interrupts transactional database instances, enterprise ERP, and operational management systems. fr.exec_narrative_p1: Every technological architecture upholds a financial promise. For {tower_name}, that promise currently rests on fragile foundations (Level {score_display} - {global_band}). Our forensic analysis reveals that the underlying infrastructure is not suffering from a lack of capacity, but rather from a silent erosion of operational resilience: structural vulnerabilities where an unpredicted fault holds the potential to sever {client_name}'s business continuity.
fr.exec_narrative_p2: To translate this technical fragility into boardroom economics, we rejected arbitrary industry averages. By applying an actuarial model calibrated against actual exposed corporate turnover ({effective_exposed_revenue_formatted} {currency_code}), we established a composite downtime burn rate of **{hourly_cost}/h** (incorporating a {sector_impact_factor_pct}% direct revenue velocity penalty, SLA breach accruals, and incident labor burden). This valuation directly links the platform's vulnerabilities with {client_name}'s operating cash flow.
fr.exec_narrative_p3: Furthermore, to prevent mathematical inflation, we deduplicated overlapping blast radii via joint failure probability: true net exposure stands at **{ale_hours} critical hours annually**, crystallizing a net Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE) of **{ale_formatted}**. Under a severe tail-risk scenario (90th percentile), an uncontrollable outage could cripple operations for up to {p90_hours} hours, incurring a catastrophic exposure of **{p90_formatted}**.
fr.exec_narrative_p4: Deferring remediation is not cost containment; it is the unhedged underwriting of an operational catastrophe. Executing the proposed target roadmap eliminates the current operational paralysis and automates resilience in {tower_name}. This capital allocation converts an unpredictable technical liability into hardened operational equity, safeguarding both {client_name}'s EBITDA and institutional trust against severe disruption.

fr.p90_callout_body_template: Consistent with the Chapter 1 executive synthesis, actuarial modeling at the 90th percentile (P90) evaluates a compound failure triggered by {compound_failure_trigger}. Under this asymptotic stress regime, the physical reconstruction, state synchronization, and operational verification window extends up to {p90_recovery_hours} hours. The projected maximum contingent financial exposure reaches {p90_total_contingency}, comprising {direct_stoppage_loss} in direct operational stoppage losses and {secondary_disaster_spend} in secondary disaster expenditures (emergency OEM vendor escalation, expedited hardware logistics, and Tier-3 specialized triage).
fr.p90_callout_p1: To evaluate the practical resilience limit of this capability tower, the model simulates a severe, plausible scenario in which multiple critical failures occur simultaneously ({compound_failure_trigger}). Unlike routine isolated incidents, this case examines the operational reality when both primary systems and their backup mechanisms fail concurrently.
fr.p90_callout_p2: In a disruption of this magnitude, recovery requires more than restarting equipment; teams must rebuild operations step by step and verify that no critical business data has been corrupted. Under current technical conditions, fully restoring service and validating data consistency would require up to {p90_recovery_hours} hours.
fr.p90_callout_p3: The total financial exposure of this scenario reaches {p90_total_contingency}. This impact breaks down clearly into two categories: {direct_stoppage_loss} in direct losses from halted commercial and operational activity during the outage, and {secondary_disaster_spend} in extraordinary emergency expenses (such as urgent third-party specialist intervention, priority vendor support, and expedited operational recovery services).

fr.sec4_1_alpha_reconciliation: Downtime Cost Scaling by Failure Scope: The baseline corporate rate ({base_rate}/h) represents a complete shutdown of all business operations. Because most technical incidents do not halt 100% of the company, the model scales the hourly cost according to the actual scope of each failure: 70% ({rate_70}/h) for core critical platforms, 40% ({rate_40}/h) for intermediate systems with partial degradation, and 20% ({rate_20}/h) for isolated peripheral components. This ensures each risk card realistically reflects the financial impact of its specific domain.
fr.sle_derivation_formula_bullet: • **Exact Financial Derivation (SLE):** {effective_hours}h operational disruption at {hourly_rate}/hr ({alpha_pct}% operational impact factor over baseline downtime cost of {base_rate}/hr) = {sle_formatted}.

fr.tomo_ch1_headline: Evaluation of Current Infrastructure and Operations at {client_name}
fr.tomo_ch1_lead_in: The transversal audit highlights four critical risk factors requiring immediate leadership action:
fr.tomo_ch1_p1: L'évaluation exhaustive du portefeuille technologique de {client} couvre {domain_count} domaines opérationnels et établit un Indice Global de Maturité de {score} sur 5.00 ({cmmi_label}). Ce profil reflète une architecture dotée de capacités consolidées sur ses actifs phares, mais exposée à des asymétries structurelles et à une concentration des risques financiers exigeant une gouvernance exécutive prioritaire.
fr.tomo_ch1_p3:
La quantification économique des risques techniques selon le standard international Open FAIR™ (Factor Analysis of Information Risk) établit trois dimensions complémentaires pour la prise de décision de la direction :

1. **Exposition Annuelle Moyenne (ALE) de {formatted_ale} annualisés :** Reflète la perte moyenne attendue au cours d'un exercice standard, cumulant la friction opérationnelle récurrente, les heures supplémentaires de support et les inefficacités de maintenance absorbées par le compte de résultat.

2. **Coût d'un Incident Majeur Unique pouvant atteindre {worst_incident_cost} :** Correspond à l'impact direct d'un arrêt critique dans le domaine le plus exposé ({worst_incident_code} - {worst_incident_domain}) lors d'une défaillance isolée de composant ou d'une indisponibilité de plateforme.

3. **Scénario de Crise Annuelle Cumulée de {formatted_p90} :** Modélise l'exposition financière globale dans l'éventualité où plusieurs incidents graves surviendraient sur différentes plateformes au cours d'un exercice défavorable.

Ce dimensionnement permet au Comité de Direction d'orienter les investissements de modernisation là où le retour sur atténuation des risques est maximal par unité de capital engagé.
fr.tomo_ch2_footnote: *Methodological note: The consolidated index of {global_score} out of 5.00 reflects the weighted average by operational criticality across domains (the simple arithmetic mean is {simple_mean}).*
fr.tomo_ch2_intro: L'évaluation de la maturité technologique détermine la capacité réelle de l'architecture actuelle à maintenir la continuité opérationnelle, à faire évoluer les processus industriels et à atténuer les risques d'interruption. Le modèle analytique audite les 10 tours technologiques selon l'échelle standard CMMI (Capability Maturity Model Integration) de 1,00 à 5,00, en se basant exclusivement sur des preuves empiriques collectées sur l'infrastructure, les applications et les processus opérationnels de l'organisation.
fr.tomo_ch2_summary: The CMMI diagnostic places {client_name} at a consolidated index of {global_score} out of 5.00 ({maturity_tier_label}), reflecting an operational foundation with established baseline capabilities alongside inter-domain disparities. Technology domains with the largest deficits against sector benchmarks require targeted modernization roadmaps to mitigate technical debt.
fr.tomo_ch3_financial_hierarchy_body:
To ensure complete transparency for the CFO and Executive Board, the model defines three complementary financial metrics:
1. **Expected Annual Loss Exposure (ALE P50):** Modeled annual operational loss exposure across all evaluated technology domains in the current state.
2. **Single Major Outage Impact (P90 Local):** Maximum loss under an unredundant technical outage halting operations across primary facilities during {duration_str} of downtime and transactional verification.
3. **Annual Aggregate Severe Portfolio Risk (P90 Annual):** The 90th percentile aggregate portfolio loss under compounding adverse operational events across all operating units.
fr.tomo_ch3_financial_hierarchy_title: Actuarial Reconciliation Framework & Metric Hierarchy (Open FAIR™)
fr.tomo_ch3_intro: To eliminate the ambiguity of subjective RAG matrices, this assessment executes the Open FAIR™ standard driven by 10,000-run Monte Carlo stochastic engines, independently evaluating Loss Event Frequency (LEF / TEF) and Loss Magnitude (SLE / LM) across structural failure vectors.
fr.tomo_ch3_p90_1: Alors que les fiches de risque détaillées à la Section 3.3 évaluent l'impact d'événements majeurs isolés, le modèle stochastique de Monte Carlo simule la queue de distribution annuelle des pertes agrégées du portefeuille.
fr.tomo_ch3_p90_2: Under an unfavorable operational year where multiple moderate and severe incidents materialize concurrently across the ten technology domains during the same budget cycle, annual aggregate portfolio losses reach {formatted_p90} at the 90th percentile (Annual P90).
fr.tomo_ch3_p90_3: This {formatted_p90} figure establishes the unprovisioned annual exposure ceiling that fully justifies the strategic technical standardization and contingency investments detailed in the target roadmap.
fr.tomo_ch3_rate: The composite hourly downtime baseline is calibrated at **{baseline_rate}**, reconciling operational loss of velocity, contractual SLA penalties, and emergency recovery burden. At operational facilities and primary delivery sites, the local hourly rate reflects the direct interruption of business transaction throughput.

fr.tomo_ch4_t10_title: 4.10. Systèmes Critiques d'Expédition et Opérations Locales (T10)
fr.tomo_ch4_t1_text: Primary technical facilities provide continuous operational support for enterprise compute and connectivity workloads. Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems and diesel backup generators maintain regular preventive maintenance, operating within conventional thermal profiles that require continuous environmental telemetry.
fr.tomo_ch4_t2_text: Core compute environments rely on virtualized platforms experiencing high memory utilization, constraining automated failover headroom during physical node maintenance windows. The platform requires a structured modernization roadmap to align hypervisor licensing with organizational growth.
fr.tomo_ch4_t3_text: The enterprise network fabric interconnects corporate headquarters, regional offices, and operational sites. Core inter-site communications leverage dedicated redundant connectivity, while distributed facilities utilize managed WAN links over secure tunnels, representing a strategic opportunity for SD-WAN convergence.
fr.tomo_ch4_t4_text: Core enterprise storage relies on Almacenamiento Centralizado FAS/AFF arrays via NFS and Fibre Channel. While operational maturity is high (CMMI Level 3), missing WORM SnapLock immutability leaves backup repositories exposed to ransomware encryption. Controller multipathing requires validation to prevent I/O bottlenecks during firmware updates.
fr.tomo_ch4_t5_text: Business continuity and disaster recovery procedures maintain secondary replications of critical data repositories, with full operational resilience requiring automated switchover testing to minimize recovery time objectives (RTO).
fr.tomo_ch4_t6_text: Perimeter security enforces firewall filtering across major ingress points. Identity governance requires federating disparate directory forests into a unified model, deploying Privileged Access Management (PAM) for administrative accounts, and deepening network segmentation.
fr.tomo_ch4_t7_text: Transactional core runs on Oracle Database and SQL Server engines with concentrated administration knowledge. The ITSM platform lacks an automated CMDB federated with the infrastructure digital twin.
fr.tomo_ch4_t8_text: Core ERP platforms and business application suites constitute the operational heart of the enterprise. Cloud workloads and SaaS software subscriptions require unified cost-allocation tagging to optimize recurring spend and eliminate licensing overlap.

fr.tomo_ch4_t9_text: Digital workplace platforms provide standardized productivity and collaboration suites across cloud endpoints, requiring unified mobile device management policies across all distributed offices.

tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Immediate shutdown of auxiliary electronics and management plane outage.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Point-to-point 10Gb DCI link between sites without redundant ring topology.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Write lock on transactional virtual machines and storage split-brain.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Compressor failure on uncontained high-density perimeter cooling unit.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Thermal server trip within 18 minutes due to hot-air recirculation.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing Tier-0 PAM bastion and brittle directory synchronization across entities.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Identity plane freeze and plant-level ERP authentication lockout.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing WORM immutability and lack of an isolated Cyber Recovery Vault.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Irreversible backup encryption or purge during enterprise ransomware outbreak.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Fibre Channel I/O paths without active multipathing across controllers.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Transactional storage freeze during firmware maintenance reboots.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: IPSec tunnels over commodity internet without dynamic SD-WAN failover.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Telemetry loss to operational dispatch systems stalling industrial product dispatch.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Core database instances without synchronous high-availability cross-site replicas.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Potential data loss and manual recovery with RTO exceeding 8 hours.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing mandatory cost-center tagging policies across public cloud tenants.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Undetected budget drift and recurring licensing overlap.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: End-of-life hardware and unsupported operating systems operating near failure.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Total plant scale shutdown with direct downtime losses of impacto operacional significativo.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Dispatch PC operating in single-phase non-redundant architecture.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Halted operational transaction processing at a burn rate of impacto operacional significativor.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Effective RTO exceeding 18 hours during major data corruption events.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Implementation of immutable WORM storage tier and cloud replication.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Accelerated CPU component aging and risk of thermal shutdown.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Installation of physical cold-aisle containment and BMS IoT sensors.
