T1.inventory: 2 technical rooms at primary headquarters, generator sets in ring topology, N+1 UPS schemes, gas fire suppression, and perimeter HVAC.
findings: Absence of hot/cold aisle aerodynamic containment causing thermal recirculation across compute racks at ASHRAE limits.
Lack of real-time IoT power telemetry on electrical panels and PDUs, preventing phase-level capacity measurement.
Absence of biometric access controls at airlocks and electronic work permits (ePtW) required for NIS2 compliance.
Lack of automated correlation between environmental sensors and fire suppression systems for adjacent containment.
Electromechanical preventive maintenance managed reactively without centralized CMMS or live-load transfer testing.
strengths: Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems in N+1 redundancy with certified preventive maintenance routines.
Precision air conditioning units (CRAC) providing environmental control across technical datacenter rooms.
Automated clean-agent fire suppression and detection deployed in primary technical spaces.
Optical and thermal fire detection zoning under raised floors and ceilings complying with engineering standards.
Monitored electrical distribution switchboards and technical alarms integrated into operations control.

T2.inventory: 3 hyperconverged nodes running legacy VMware ESXi and Windows/Linux server workloads with mixed cloud instances.
findings: Structural CPU and memory saturation (>90%) preventing N+1 failover between technical rooms without workload degradation.
Absence of a unified corporate managed Kubernetes platform with security guardrails and service mesh.
Fragmented public cloud adoption lacking automated Landing Zone governance and policy enforcement guardrails.
Absence of declarative Infrastructure as Code (IaC) pipelines for continuous provisioning and version tracking.
Absence of Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) telemetry linked to core business flows.
strengths: Centralized hyperconverged compute cluster delivering dense processing capacity for corporate workloads.
Standardized operating system base templates and container execution environments for microservices.
Production hosting of mission-critical workloads (SAP S/4HANA) on Tier-1 enterprise hyperscalers (GCP/Azure).
Automated virtual server cloning and baseline deployment procedures across primary clusters.
Hypervisor-level automated high availability (HA) failover operational across compute nodes.

T3.inventory: Dual-core switching infrastructure, perimeter firewalls, and SD-WAN links interconnecting 18 operating country sites.
findings: Access layer switches across remote quarries and industrial plants approaching commercial End-of-Life (EoL).
Secondary plant interconnects dependent on static IPSec tunnels lacking dynamic traffic steering and SD-WAN failover.
Point-to-point Data Center Interconnect (DCI) lacking physical ring topology and exterior conduit diversification.
Cloud interconnect architecture lacking centralized transit routing (Cloud Router) and automated multi-region failover.
Manual network administration via CLI without declarative NetDevOps workflows or version-controlled configurations.
strengths: Dual-core backbone switching infrastructure with redundant uplinks across technical distribution frames.
Corporate WAN and SD-WAN connectivity established across manufacturing plants, quarries, and branch offices.
Dedicated high-speed 10 Gbps point-to-point fiber interconnecting primary operational datacenters.
High-performance direct interconnect ports linking core routing to public cloud transit hubs.
Centralized bandwidth monitoring probes and active link telemetry supervised in network consoles.

T4.inventory: Enterprise SAN arrays and NAS clusters replicating asynchronously across dual technical rooms.
findings: Lack of native Calidad de Servicio (QoS) bandwidth shaping on SAN arrays, exposing critical databases to I/O noisy neighbors.
Fragmented audit logging on storage controllers without dedicated write-once-read-many (WORM) audit vaults.
Reliance on local snapshot copies without physical cyber isolation against targeted ransomware encryption campaigns.
Absence of strict WORM immutability (SnapLock) activation across mission-critical volume snapshots for NIS2 compliance.
Operational friction and blurred boundary delineation in storage administration between internal IT and external support.
subpillars: Security & Access Controls for Data Platforms
strengths: High-performance enterprise storage arrays featuring dynamic capacity allocation and thin-provisioning.
Storage capacity thresholds monitored with proactive alert notifications in central dashboards.
Scheduled snapshot policies and asynchronous block-level replication between active datacenters.
Protected enterprise storage volumes configured with accidental deletion safeguards and data-at-rest encryption.
Native SAN storage volume integration supporting corporate hypervisor clusters.

T5.inventory: Tape-based and disk backup targets with manual disaster recovery playbooks and scheduled off-site replication.
findings: Concentration of datacenter resilience within a shared geographic perimeter, creating a geographic Single Point of Failure.
Technical recovery times (RTO > 4 hours) exceeding operational tolerance thresholds for continuous core transaction processing.
Absence of scheduled, full-scale disaster recovery exercises (game days) under live production mains power disconnection.
Absence of an isolated Cyber Recovery Vault with automated forensic data validation prior to mass restore execution.
Lack of symmetric standby capacity across twin datacenters preventing transparent workload failover without shutdown.
strengths: Documented contingency and disaster recovery operational procedures for essential industrial systems.
Scheduled disk and tape backup policies with verified off-site custody procedures.
Skilled internal engineering team possessing deep operational experience in manual plant system restoration.
Air-gapped offline magnetic tape backups maintained in physically isolated custody facilities.
Local electromechanical component redundancy and automated core server service failover.

T6.inventory: Centralized Active Directory domains, endpoint EDR agents, and outsourced SOC monitoring alerts.
findings: Identity plane fragmentation and persistence of over-privileged static administrative credentials lacking dynamic JIT elevation.
Absence of an enterprise Privileged Access Management (PAM) vault enforcing automated credential rotation and session monitoring.
Infrequent security configuration baseline audits lacking automated configuration drift detection across systems.
Partial vulnerability scanning coverage omitting legacy virtual machines, industrial gateways, and acquired subsidiaries.
Flat industrial plant network topology lacking East-West microsegmentation, allowing undetected threat propagation.
strengths: Centralized enterprise identity and access management directory (Active Directory).
Enforced corporate password complexity policies and initial administrative role segregation.
Homogeneous endpoint detection and response (EDR) agent deployment with external SOC monitoring.
Scheduled external perimeter penetration scanning and corporate operating system update cycles.
Next-generation perimeter firewalls enforcing corporate network traffic filtering and secure VPN.

T7.inventory: Relational database clusters (SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL) and central ITSM ticketing platform.
findings: Misalignment between technical infrastructure SLAs and core manufacturing operations, obscuring plant-level outage impact.
Manual incident triage and dispatch workflows lacking intelligent routing based on industrial operational criticality.
Absence of an automated, federated Configuration Management Database (CMDB) maintaining live dependency maps.
Reactive root cause analysis (RCA) procedures lacking institutionalized Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) error budgets.
Fragmented monitoring tooling lacking cross-domain causal event correlation between on-premise, cloud, and OT environments.
strengths: Documented IT service catalog and service level agreements (SLAs) established for internal business units.
Centralized IT Service Management (ITSM) ticketing platform structuring operational incidents and requests.
Centralized hardware and software license inventory maintained by the IT infrastructure department.
Structured post-incident reviews conducted following major service outages to identify direct causes.
Core infrastructure telemetry probes (CPU, memory, storage, ping) transmitting alerts to central consoles.

T8.inventory: ERP applications (SAP), logistics management platforms, and multi-cloud SaaS subscriptions.
findings: Critical architectural obsolescence across legacy operating systems and database engines lacking budgeted modernization paths.
Asymmetric governance between corporate headquarters and newly acquired subsidiaries, perpetuating operational silos.
Absence of continuous, quantified technical risk governance modeled under Open FAIR standards.
Reactive cloud financial governance lacking automated resource tagging enforcement and showback/chargeback models.
Absence of executive dashboards correlating technology investments with measurable plant productivity gains.
subpillars: Value Realization, Executive Metrics & Continuous Improvement
strengths: Strategic technology roadmap aligned with corporate business growth and digital modernization goals.
Periodic IT governance committee and structured capital expenditure approval processes.
Formal corporate information security policies and accounting/tax compliance oversight.
Centralized monthly billing visibility within multi-cloud consoles (GCP, Azure, and OCI).
Consolidated IT operational expenditure metrics tracked for senior financial leadership.

T9.inventory: Managed Windows 11 and macOS corporate endpoints, Microsoft 365 productivity suite, and mobile MDM profiles.
findings: Plant and quarry endpoint devices administered locally without centralized modern device management enrollment.
Vulnerability across shared industrial plant workstations lacking passwordless biometric or FIDO2 authentication.
Document sprawl across unmanaged cloud repositories lacking automated lifecycle and data retention governance policies.
Manual endpoint provisioning and workstation support processes increasing fulfillment lead times across remote facilities.
Absence of Digital Employee Experience (DEX) real-time telemetry for proactive degradation and latency detection.
subpillars: Productividad, Colaboración y Gestión del Conocimiento
strengths: Standardized corporate endpoint fleet operating under unified modern management baselines.
Secure remote connectivity and multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled for knowledge workers.
Cloud collaboration and productivity suites (M365) widely adopted across business units.
Structured Level-1 service desk and automated operating system security patch distribution.
Direct communication channels and periodic user satisfaction surveys conducted by the IT team.

T10.inventory: Mission-critical core processing engines, enterprise clearing interfaces, and operational transactional platforms.
findings: Core transactional terminals and processing engines operating on outdated hardware configurations and legacy operating systems.
Software modifications on legacy transactional components applied manually without version control in Git repositories.
Batch processing queues and data transfers concentrated in peak operating windows causing storage controller I/O spikes.
Direct database-level point-to-point links between legacy and modern systems lacking governed API contracts.
Critical dependence on tacit operational knowledge held by specialized personnel approaching retirement on legacy stacks.
strengths: Core transactional processing engines maintained with verified operational stability and scheduled maintenance.
Robust, well-rehearsed manual dispatch continuity procedures during communication disruptions.
Automated transactional synchronization interfaces transferring event logs and clearing records to central enterprise ERP.
Functional point-to-point integration connectors guaranteeing dispatch and billing continuity.
Dedicated and highly qualified on-site operational staff ensuring resilient local execution.

fr.tomo_triad_bottleneck_desc: Operational reliance on manual interventions by internal engineering teams and facility vulnerability during network degradation.
fr.tomo_triad_gap_desc: High resource pressure across core clusters (>90%), baseline operational telemetry, and upcoming software contract renewals requiring strategic consolidation.
fr.tomo_triad_strength_desc: Robust mechanical fire suppression across technical facilities alongside centralized structured storage.

fr.tomo_ch1_continuity_bullet_body: Les systèmes et services sur les sites opérationnels dépendent de liaisons de communication uniques et d'équipements en fin de support, exposant l'activité quotidienne à des interruptions techniques lors d'incidents locaux.

fr.tomo_ch2_benchmark_methodology_body: La référence reflète la médiane empirique (P50) du secteur de l'industrie lourde, reconnaissant l'asymétrie réelle entre les services informatiques banalisés et la continuité opérationnelle en usine.
fr.tomo_ch2_benchmark_methodology_title: Méthodologie d'Étalonnage de la Référence Sectorielle (Médiane P50)
fr.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_1: • Out-of-Contract 24x7 OEM Emergency Engineering Intervention ({bucket_1_cost} — {bucket_1_pct} of emergency spend): Reactive engagement of Tier-3 Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specialists at emergency Time & Materials rates outside standard SLAs to rebuild hypervisors, storage arrays, or network switches whose standard support has lapsed.
fr.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_2: • Urgent Spot-Market Hardware Procurement and Dedicated Courier Logistics ({bucket_2_cost} — {bucket_2_pct} of emergency spend): Immediate spot-market purchase of replacement servers, controllers, drives, or switches at premium availability pricing, combined with dedicated same-day air/ground courier transport directly to affected facilities.
fr.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_3: • Specialized Database Recovery and Level-3 Forensic Triage Services ({bucket_3_cost} — {bucket_3_pct} of emergency spend): Engagement of external recovery engineers specialized in repairing corrupted transactional tables (core ERP/corporate databases), reconciling in-flight transactions interrupted by the crash, and performing forensic containment prior to production restart.
fr.tomo_ch3_exec_intro_p1: Ce chapitre quantifie l'impact financier et les risques opérationnels de l'architecture actuelle selon le standard international Open FAIR™. Son objectif est de fournir à la Direction des Systèmes d'Information et au Comité de Direction une base objective et économiquement défendable sur le coût réel d'exploitation de l'infrastructure dans son état actuel. Pour ce faire, le modèle identifie et priorise les principaux scénarios de défaillance technique en fonction de leur probabilité et de leur gravité, évaluant tant la perte récurrente absorbée au quotidien par le compte de résultat que la facture directe à laquelle l'entreprise ferait face lors d'incidents majeurs ou de crises cumulées.
fr.tomo_ch3_sec31_reconciliation_bridge: Pour faciliter l'arbitrage budgétaire et la priorisation des investissements par la Direction, le tableau suivant consolide la corrélation directe entre la maturité technique et le risque financier de chaque domaine, détaillant la perte annuelle attendue (ALE), le coût d'une défaillance sévère isolée et la part d'exposition sur l'ensemble du portefeuille :

This {total_emergency_cost} expenditure decomposes into three auditable operational buckets:

Business Interruption and Direct Operational Stoppage ({direct_stoppage_loss}): Represents the direct business burn rate across {outage_duration_hours} of downtime at {consolidated_hourly_rate}. This encompasses halted shipments, stalled dispatch lines, idle operational labor hours, and delayed order processing and billing.

fr.tomo_ch3_step2_sub1_intro: When a severe failure strikes critical infrastructure (such as a primary virtualization cluster collapse or core storage corruption without immutable backups), the estimated mean time to rebuild the environment, restore data volumes, and verify transactional integrity reaches {outage_duration_hours}. An incident of this magnitude generates an estimated total financial impact of {total_event_loss}, divided into two distinct operational components:

fr.tomo_ch4_spof_section_intro: The following matrix consolidates the 10 single points of failure identified across the current architecture, sorted in descending order of operational criticality to focus remediation investments on the most severe operational threats:
fr.tomo_ch4_spof_section_title: 4.11. Consolidated Single Point of Failure (SPOF) Matrix
fr.tomo_ch3_p90_4: Sur un horizon cumulé de 3 ans sans remédiation architecturale, la perte attendue s'élève à {var_3y_expected}, atteignant une valeur à risque cumulée à 3 ans (VaR 3Y P90) de {var_3y_tail} sous stress opérationnel continu.
fr.tomo_ch3_loss_composition_note: Note méthodologique sur la composition de l'impact : Selon la méthodologie Open FAIR™, les pertes annualisées modélisées ne représentent pas uniquement des coûts indirects de productivité. Lors d'incidents majeurs, environ 50% de l'exposition se traduit par des décaissements directs d'urgence.
fr.tomo_ch2_summary_p1: L'indice global consolidé de maturité s'établit à {overall_maturity} sur 5,00, positionnant la plateforme technologique au Niveau 2 (Répétable). Ce résultat reflète une architecture à deux vitesses clairement différenciées. D'une part, les capacités de base de l'entreprise — Stockage et Sauvegarde (3,30) et Poste de Travail Numérique (3,10) — ont atteint le Niveau 3 (Défini), fonctionnant selon des normes documentées, des architectures centralisées et des niveaux de service prévisibles.
fr.tomo_ch2_summary_p2: D'autre part, les domaines soutenant l'exécution industrielle et transactionnelle — Continuité Opérationnelle (2,10), Applications Métier (2,40) et Systèmes d'Expédition (2,40) — restent ancrés dans la tranche réactive du Niveau 2. Dans ces domaines, la stabilité opérationnelle repose sur l'effort réactif des équipes techniques, des configurations locales sans redondance automatisée et des intégrations point à point. Cette asymétrie structurelle constitue le vecteur principal d'exposition opérationnelle et financière analysé au Chapitre 3.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T1: Centres de données avec robustesse mécanique solide, limités par le confinement thermique et la télémétrie électrique basique.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T2: Stable core virtualization and hyperconverged platforms, constrained by high memory pressure and upcoming technological refresh milestones.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T3: Topologie WAN/SD-WAN opérationnelle, avec nécessité de renforcer la segmentation IT/OT et la double adduction sur carrières clés.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T4: Architecture de stockage et sauvegarde centralisée et prévisible, avec politiques formelles de rétention et réplication.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T5: Procédures PRA non formalisées en usine, forte dépendance aux interventions manuelles et délais de reprise prolongés.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T6: Contrôles de sécurité périmétrique actifs, nécessitant une visibilité accrue sur les réseaux OT et le déploiement du PAM.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T7: Gestion stable des bases de données transactionnelles, en attente de standardisation des correctifs et gouvernance ITSM.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T8: Écosystème SAP/ERP consolidé en finance, pénalisé par des intégrations satellites manuelles et contrats fragmentés.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T9: Environnement bureautique et poste de travail standardisé sous Microsoft 365, avec une gouvernance mature.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_T10: Local operations and distributed facility support with operational continuity processes reliant on manual procedures.
fr.tomo_ch2_driver_summary: Asymétrie structurelle entre services corporatifs standardisés (Niveau 3) et opérations d'usine exposées (Niveau 2).

fr.gloss_erc_high: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - High]:** High structural influence; a critical outage in this domain easily propagates cascades destabilizing connected enterprise systems.
fr.gloss_erc_medium: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Medium]:** Moderate structural influence; disruption remains contained, impacting only immediately adjacent workloads.
fr.gloss_erc_low: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Low/Isolated]:** Low structural influence; failures remain strictly isolated within this technical perimeter without holding-wide impact.
fr.gloss_mcda_crit_extreme: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Extreme]:** Assesses the level of direct dependency that key operational processes have on this domain. Core business operations depend critically on this platform, and an outage would cause immediate disruption of essential services.
fr.gloss_mcda_crit_high: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - High]:** Reflects high operational dependency, though a brief latency tolerance exists before core business continuity is disrupted.
fr.gloss_mcda_crit_medium: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Medium]:** The domain provides supportive or back-office services whose temporary downtime is manageable via standard contingency procedures.
fr.gloss_mcda_reg_critical: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Critical]:** Severe regulatory exposure under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001), where security deficiencies directly incur high statutory penalties and direct corporate liability.
fr.gloss_mcda_reg_moderate: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Moderate]:** Strict corporate compliance and security baseline mandates apply, requiring periodic independent IT control audits.
fr.gloss_mcda_reg_standard: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Standard]:** Standard operational compliance based on engineering best practices without direct statutory critical scrutiny.
fr.gloss_mcda_viab_favorable: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Feasible]:** Transformation feasibility is favorable. Modernization initiatives can be delivered with mature technologies and market resources without critical disruption.
fr.gloss_mcda_viab_complex: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Complex]:** High execution complexity due to structural technical debt, maintenance bottlenecks, or specialized skill scarcity.
fr.gloss_dii_high: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Stability]:** The extremely low Decision Instability Index mathematically certifies that findings are robust and unaffected by small evidence variations.
fr.gloss_dii_moderate: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - Moderate Stability]:** Moderate sensitivity; findings are substantially stable though specific sub-scores depend on evolving architectural interpretation.
fr.gloss_dii_volatile: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Sensitivity]:** High volatility; limited evidentiary backing suggests further confirmation is required to lock target maturity scores.
fr.executive_summary_narrative_default: Feuille de route de modernisation technologique d'entreprise établie pour consolider la résilience opérationnelle et la vélocité stratégique dans tous les domaines fonctionnels.

fr.forensic_finding_fallback_template: Déficit de contrôle dans {lowest_subpillar_name} (indice de maturité {lowest_subpillar_score}/{max_cmmi_str}).
fr.tomo_ch3_table4_footnote: * Critère d'Agrégation Actuarielle : L'Exposition Annuelle Attendue (ALE) est additive entre domaines, tandis que les coûts par incident majeur représentent des contingences opérationnelles indépendantes. Par rigueur technique, la ligne de synthèse n'effectue pas de somme arithmétique, mais reflète l'impact du scénario critique le plus sévère ({worst_incident_cost} sur {worst_incident_code} — {worst_incident_domain}), tandis que l'exposition de crise cumulée du portefeuille est modélisée de manière stochastique à {formatted_p90}.
fr.tomo_polarity_section_title: 1.1. Domaines Clés : Forces et Points Critiques
fr.tomo_polarity_leader_desc: Plus haut niveau de contrôle ({leader_score} / 5.00). Bénéficie d'un support actif, d'une redondance opérationnelle et sert de modèle interne.
fr.tomo_polarity_risk_desc: Concentre {top_risk_share_pct}% du risque financier total ({top_risk_ale} / an). Une panne dans ce domaine bloque les processus critiques d'exploitation et de facturation.
fr.tomo_polarity_lagging_desc: Plus faible niveau de maturité ({lagging_score} / 5.00). Fonctionne avec une forte dépendance manuelle sans capacité de reprise automatique.
fr.tomo_ch2_sec2_intro: La maturité est notée sur une échelle analytique de 1,00 à 5,00 segmentée en intervalles continus de 0,80 point, où chaque niveau définit un seuil de contrôle opérationnel et de gouvernance :
fr.tomo_ch2_scale_col_criteria: Poste de Contrôle Opérationnel et de Gouvernance
fr.tomo_ch2_scale_lvl1_desc: Pratiques réactives et ad hoc, avec une dépendance critique envers l'effort individuel du personnel clé.
fr.tomo_ch2_scale_lvl2_desc: Processus opérationnels de base établis au niveau tactique, mais avec des silos et des incohérences entre sites.
fr.tomo_ch2_scale_lvl3_desc: Standards formalisés, documentés et appliqués de manière homogène dans toute l'organisation.
fr.tomo_ch2_scale_lvl4_desc: Capacités mesurées quantitativement, avec télémétrie opérationnelle et plein alignement sur la gouvernance informatique.
fr.tomo_ch2_scale_lvl5_desc: Modèle d'excellence opérationnelle, avec automatisation avancée et cycles systématiques d'amélioration continue.
fr.tomo_ch3_tier_table_intro: Pour faciliter la priorisation opérationnelle et l'allocation budgétaire, le modèle stratifie l'exposition de l'entreprise en trois niveaux de criticité selon l'urgence d'intervention et la nature de l'impact financier (distinguant les coûts directs d'arrêt d'exploitation et de remplacement d'urgence des inefficacités récurrentes de maintenance) :
fr.sec_3_2_taxonomy_table_title: Tableau 3.2.B — Légende de la Matrice Open FAIR™ et Regroupement Dynamique par Taxonomie de Risque
fr.sec_3_2_taxonomy_bridge_narrative: Traçabilité Actuarielle et Réconciliation Forensique : Pour traduire les {total_plot_points} vecteurs macroscopiques positionnés sur la matrice Open FAIR™ 5x5 en gouvernance exécutive actionnable, le moteur regroupe dynamiquement les {total_findings} constatations empiriques ({critical_count} Critiques, {high_count} Élevées, {medium_count} Moyennes) en {active_cluster_count} familles actives ordonnées par Perte Annuelle Attendue (ALE).
fr.sec_3_2_col_taxonomy_family: Famille Taxonomique de Risque Systémique (ORX / FAIR)
fr.sec_3_2_col_systemic_threat_rationale: Menace Métier Exécutive et Périmètre Empirique Audité
fr.sec_3_2_row_total_rationale: Réconciliation mathématique à 100% entre les annexes forensiques des N domaines et les vecteurs de la matrice exécutive.
fr.TAXONOMY_STRUCTURAL_OBSOLESCENCE_RATIONA: Fragilité opérationnelle et exposition non corrigée liée aux infrastructures en fin de vie (EoL), aux noyaux obsolètes et au couplage monolithique
fr.TAXONOMY_CYBER_IDENTITY_GOVERNANCE_TITLE: Cyber-Résilience, Gouvernance des Identités et Périmètre
fr.TAXONOMY_CYBER_IDENTITY_GOVERNANCE_RATIO: Mouvement latéral non autorisé, élévation de privilèges et non-conformité réglementaire sur les contrôles d'accès et de périmètre
fr.TAXONOMY_OPERATIONAL_CONTINUITY_EDGE_TIT: Continuité Opérationnelle, Résilience Réseau et Bordure (Edge)
fr.TAXONOMY_OPERATIONAL_CONTINUITY_EDGE_RAT: Arrêt de production et interruption de revenus dus aux points de défaillance uniques (SPOF), aux déficits de PCA/PRA ou à l'instabilité réseau
fr.TAXONOMY_PROCESS_AUTOMATION_FRICTION_TIT: Friction des Processus, Opérations Manuelles et Gouvernance
fr.TAXONOMY_PROCESS_AUTOMATION_FRICTION_RAT: Goulots d'étranglement opérationnels, taux d'échec des changements et exposition à l'erreur humaine liés aux flux manuels et aux silos ITSM
fr.TAXONOMY_DATA_INTEGRITY_ANALYTICS_TITLE: Intégrité des Données, Observabilité et Cécité Décisionnelle
fr.TAXONOMY_DATA_INTEGRITY_ANALYTICS_RATION: Rapports faussés, angles morts de télémétrie et fragmentation des données de référence dégradant le pilotage opérationnel
fr.TAXONOMY_VENDOR_ECOSYSTEM_CONCENTRATION_: Concentration Fournisseurs, Risque SLA et Licences
Dépendance commerciale exclusive, asymétrie contractuelle et passifs opérationnels ou de licences tiers non maîtrisés
fr.tomo_ch3_stress_table_intro: Pour offrir à la Direction une vision complète de l'exposition financière selon différents horizons de risque, le tableau suivant synthétise les résultats de la simulation actuarielle de Monte Carlo, confrontant le scénario d'exploitation ordinaire aux défaillances extrêmes et aux pertes cumulées sur trois ans :
fr.tomo_ch3_stress_col_desc: Définition Actuarielle et Impact Opérationnel Métier
fr.tomo_ch3_stress_row1_desc: Perte annuelle attendue liée aux frictions opérationnelles récurrentes, aux heures supplémentaires et aux inefficacités de maintenance.
fr.tomo_ch3_stress_row2_title: Incident Majeur Isolé le Plus Sévère
fr.tomo_ch3_stress_row2_desc: Impact direct d'un arrêt critique sur le domaine le plus exposé ({worst_incident_code} — {worst_incident_domain}) lors d'une panne majeure d'infrastructure.
fr.tomo_ch3_stress_row3_desc: Plafond d'exposition stochastique annuelle non provisionnée au 90e percentile en cas d'incidents sévères multiples au cours d'un même exercice.
fr.tomo_ch3_stress_row4_title: Valeur à Risque sur 3 Ans (VaR 3Y P90)
fr.tomo_ch3_stress_row4_desc: Perte cumulée sur le cycle stratégique sans mise en œuvre du plan directeur, combinant attrition quotidienne et contingences de crise.

fr.sec_3_2_detailed_diagnostics_intro: La section suivante présente l évaluation technique et procédurale exhaustive pour chacune des capacités évaluées dans ce domaine. Chaque fiche met en contraste l auto-évaluation initiale avec les preuves empiriques d audit, justifiant objectivement la maturité factuelle attribuée et établissant la trajectoire pragmatique de modernisation vers le niveau supérieur.
fr.callout_trajectory_title: Trajectoire de Maturité vers le Niveau {target_level} ({target_label}) :
fr.diag_rationale_divergence_gap: L auto-évaluation initiale de l organisation projetait un score de {dec_fmt} sur 5,0. Cependant, la vérification technique et les preuves forensiques constatent {finding_clause}. Par conséquent, l audit calibre la maturité opérationnelle à {score_fmt} ({band_label}) afin d asseoir objectivement les priorités de modernisation dans le Volume 2.
fr.diag_rationale_divergence_conservative: L exploitation technique observée dépasse l auto-évaluation déclarée ({dec_fmt}), calibrant la capacité à {score_fmt} ({band_label}). Bien que l environnement fonctionne avec stabilité, on identifie {finding_clause}, ce qui définit la marge de progression.
fr.diag_rationale_divergence_aligned: L auto-évaluation initiale ({dec_fmt}) et le diagnostic technique concordent pleinement pour situer la capacité à {score_fmt} ({band_label}). La base installée soutient l exploitation quotidienne ; néanmoins, la résilience est conditionnée par {finding_clause}.
fr.diag_rationale_fact_first_low: La gestion de cette capacité se situe dans un régime initial ({score_fmt} sur 5,0 - {band_label}). L exploitation est contrainte par {finding_clause}, imposant des contrôles fondamentaux au Volume 2.
fr.diag_rationale_fact_first_mid: La capacité fonctionne avec une stabilité quotidienne dans un régime {band_label} ({score_fmt} sur 5,0). Toutefois, la résilience est limitée par {finding_clause}, traçant la trajectoire de consolidation.
fr.diag_rationale_fact_first_high: La capacité démontre une maturité consolidée ({score_fmt} sur 5,0 - {band_label}), appuyée sur des procédures standardisées. L opportunité d optimisation porte sur {finding_clause}.

ch3_intro_by_tower.T1: The evaluation of the {tower_title} domain across {client_name} examines electromechanical resilience, physical capacity, and critical facilities stability. This chapter documents the technical diagnosis of computer rooms and processing facilities, auditing uninterrupted power continuity, environmental cooling controls, and preventative maintenance governance over core operational assets.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T2: This chapter documents the architectural assessment of compute platforms, virtualization hypervisors, and hybrid execution environments comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The diagnosis examines cluster sizing and bin-packing capacity, CPU and memory contention, and guest operating system lifecycle management against modern decoupling paradigms.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T3: This chapter analyzes communications architecture, campus networks, and wide-area interconnection links comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The audit evaluates topological resilience against transport failures, microsegmentation and perimeter controls across trust boundaries, and latency stability across corporate services and distributed operating sites.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T4: This chapter addresses the technical diagnosis of enterprise storage platforms, primary arrays, and secondary backup repositories comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation audits database performance and latency SLA compliance, immutable ransomware protection and air-gapping defenses, and storage lifecycle capacity governance.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T5: This chapter examines the operational resilience and disaster recovery posture (BC/DR) governing {tower_title} across {client_name}. The analysis contrasts technical failover and recovery procedures against business disruption tolerances, evaluating physical facility independence, core data protection, and site operational autonomy during central outages.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T6: This section presents the evaluation of the cybersecurity posture, identity governance, and infrastructure defenses comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The diagnostic audits privileged access controls (PAM), threat detection and telemetry visibility, system hardening, and compliance with enterprise security and regulatory frameworks.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T7: This chapter evaluates service delivery maturity, operational technical support, and observability workflows comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The audit examines change control discipline, configuration management database (CMDB) accuracy, incident resolution efficacy, and proactive operational event correlation.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T8: This chapter examines the fiduciary model, technological financial transparency, and strategic technology governance comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation analyzes infrastructure cost predictability and showback across business units, software licensing optimization, and technological investment alignment with organizational priorities.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T9: This chapter addresses the diagnosis of the digital workplace, collaboration solutions, and user endpoint fleets comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The analysis evaluates device fleet standardization and homogeneity, automated lifecycle staging and patching, digital employee experience (DEX), and secure endpoint access across distributed workspaces.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T10: This chapter analyzes dedicated operational platforms, activity execution systems, and field peripherals underpinning {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation audits hardware resilience at critical operating points, transactional continuity during network contingencies, and the modernization posture of core operational systems.

fr.scorecard_commentary_low: Scoring a technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_name} domain across {client_name} operates under acute operational exposure. Gaps in engineering formalization and automation are critically concentrated within {weakest_pillar_name} ({weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), constraining overall domain resilience and mandating prioritized structural remediation.
fr.scorecard_commentary_mid: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_name} domain across {client_name} sustains baseline operations through largely manual and reactive procedures. The primary technical bottleneck lies within {weakest_pillar_name} ({weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), representing the core standardization priority to prevent operational scaling from outstripping team capacity.
fr.scorecard_commentary_high: With a consolidated technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_name} domain across {client_name} operates upon a dependable, structured engineering baseline. The primary strategic challenge is not basic survival, but maximizing efficiency and optimizing {weakest_pillar_name} ({weakest_pillar_score}/5.0) to deliver high-velocity business capabilities.
fr.scorecard_contrast_single: Achieving a technical maturity score of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the evaluated capability of {weakest_pillar_name} across {client_name} governs the domain's operational posture, requiring direct alignment with organizational service objectives.
fr.scorecard_contrast_divergent_mid: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_title} domain across {client_name} sustains baseline operations through functional but largely manual procedures. Operational stability demonstrated in {strongest_pillar_name} ({strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with the technical bottleneck in {weakest_pillar_name} ({weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), defining the critical standardization boundary needed to scale reliably.
fr.scorecard_contrast_divergent_low: Scoring a technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_title} domain across {client_name} operates under acute operational exposure. While procedural progress is evident in {strongest_pillar_name} ({strongest_pillar_score}/5.0), overall resilience is critically undermined by deficiencies in {weakest_pillar_name} ({weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), mandating prioritized structural remediation.
fr.scorecard_contrast_divergent_high: With a consolidated technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_title} domain across {client_name} operates upon an established, disciplined engineering baseline. The maturity demonstrated in {strongest_pillar_name} ({strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) provides an enduring foundation, shifting the strategic challenge to optimizing efficiency and resolving residual friction in {weakest_pillar_name} ({weakest_pillar_score}/5.0) to maximize enterprise value.
fr.scorecard_contrast_uniform: Achieving a technical maturity score of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the {tower_title} domain across {client_name} exhibits an even maturity distribution across all evaluated capabilities. The strategic focus must center on elevating engineering standardization and automation across the entire domain.

ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T1: Scoring a technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), datacenter facilities across {client_name} sit at the threshold of Level 3. Solid electromechanical power and fire suppression defenses ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrast with thermal fragility in processing rooms ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where uncontained thermal zones and uneven cooling distribution introduce localized operational risk.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T2: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), compute infrastructure operates at its physical limits across {client_name}. Baseline hypervisor stability ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with compute resource saturation ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), eliminating the resilience buffer required to absorb host failure without disrupting core business transactions.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T3: Network infrastructure achieves a technical score of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}). Campus switching resilience across primary sites ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with the gap in automation and observability ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where manual configuration workflows and telemetry blindspots impede agile fault isolation across remote locations.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T4: Rated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), corporate storage demonstrates dependable snapshot replication ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0). The critical challenge lies within storage tiering architecture ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where the absence of immutable ransomware vaults and restrictive disk provisioning force technical staff at {client_name} into continuous manual quota containment.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T5: Scoring {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), operational resilience exhibits a critical gap against enterprise recovery tolerances across {client_name}. Operational backup reliability ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with continuous recovery fragility ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where insufficient geographic independence between redundant systems leaves services vulnerable to systemic regional disruption.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T6: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), cybersecurity governance operates under structured operational controls across {client_name}. While perimeter and telemetry defenses demonstrate verified maturity ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0), continuous privileged access governance and secrets automation ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0) remain critical priorities to sustain regulatory compliance.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T7: Scoring a technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), IT service management operates reactively across {client_name}. System monitoring visibility ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with the absence of formal problem management ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), consuming critical engineering capacity in recurring incident troubleshooting.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T8: Technology governance achieves a score of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}). Disciplined procurement control across {client_name} ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) coexists with cost allocation opacity ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where uncoordinated cloud commitments and software licensing constraints restrict compute scalability.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T9: With a consolidated maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the digital workplace exhibits structured hardware fleet management ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0). The primary friction lies within workplace operations and support ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where unstandardized workstation configurations and manual provisioning introduce operational overhead across {client_name}.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T10: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), core transactional processing platforms represent a critical operational dependency across {client_name}. Established transaction processing stability ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with legacy interface rigidity ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where monolithic batch architectures and tightly coupled integrations constrain operational agility.

annex_ch4_context_gamma.cloud_native: Topologie FinOps Cloud-Native (γ={gamma:.2f}): L'exposition financière provient de la dérive de calcul élastique à la demande, des instances réservées sous-optimisées et des ressources cloud orphelines.
annex_ch4_context_gamma.on_prem: Gouvernance de l'Infrastructure et Licences par Cœur (γ={gamma:.2f}): L'inefficacité se concentre sur la capacité hyperconvergée inutilisée, les licences de virtualisation par cœur et l'amortissement du matériel.
annex_ch4_context_gamma.hybrid: Arbitrage Cloud Hybride et Dimensionnement Edge (γ={gamma:.2f}): La friction financière provient des coûts d'exploitation hybrides et des engagements contractuels asymétriques.

annex_ch4_context_beta.clinical: Vulnérabilité Clinique Aiguë (β={beta:.2f}): La télémétrie des soins intensifs fonctionne avec une tolérance tampon quasi nulle, répercutant l'arrêt directement sur la prise en charge médicale.
annex_ch4_context_beta.synchronous: Sensibilité de Compensation Synchrone (β={beta:.2f}): Les flux de paiement fonctionnent sans tampon, déclenchant le rejet immédiat des transactions et des pénalités de SLA.
annex_ch4_context_beta.high_tempo: Exposition Opérationnelle à Haut Rythme (β={beta:.2f}): La disponibilité continue est critique pour éviter l'interruption immédiate des opérations et la perte directe de revenus.
annex_ch4_context_beta.buffered_silo: Tampon Physique par Silos et Stocks (β={beta:.2f}): La production et l'expédition sont partiellement protégées par des stocks intermédiaires en silos, évitant une perte financière linéaire lors des pannes courtes.

fr.p90_callout_finops_p1: Pour évaluer la limite de résilience budgétaire de ce domaine, le modèle simule un scénario sévère où coïncident de multiples écarts contractuels et architecturaux: {trigger_text}.
fr.p90_callout_finops_p2: Face à une dérive budgétaire d'une telle ampleur, la régularisation nécessite de renégocier les engagements pluriannuels et d'auditer les ressources orphelines. Stabiliser les dépenses nécessiterait jusqu'à {p90_rec_hours_str} mois.
fr.p90_callout_finops_p3: L'exposition financière totale de ce scénario atteint {p90_contingency_str}, ventilée en: {direct_stoppage_str} en surcoûts directs de calcul à la demande et {secondary_spend_str} en régularisations de licences et conseil FinOps spécialisé.
fr.ch4_tier1_focus_capital_inefficiency: Imminent software license true-up liabilities, contract renewals, and cumulative on-demand cloud budget drift.
fr.ch4_tier2_focus_capital_inefficiency: Oversized compute allocations, orphaned cloud resources, and lack of business unit cost allocation (showback).
fr.ch4_tier3_focus_capital_inefficiency: Decentralized SaaS sprawl and micro-subscription billing inefficiencies.
fr.ch4_tier1_focus_regulatory_and_breach: Critical exploitable vulnerabilities, lack of IT/OT segmentation, and major regulatory penalty exposure.
fr.ch4_tier2_focus_regulatory_and_breach: Gaps in continuous security monitoring (SIEM/SOC), privileged access management (PAM), and incident response.
fr.ch4_tier3_focus_regulatory_and_breach: Procedural compliance gaps and minor documentation drift without direct technical exploitability.
fr.ch4_tier1_focus_productivity_toil: Operational bottlenecks and tool failures that halt service delivery or broadly disrupt end users.
fr.ch4_tier2_focus_productivity_toil: Repetitive manual support toil, inefficient triage workflows, and absence of automated remediation.
fr.ch4_tier3_focus_productivity_toil: Self-service friction and localized fulfillment delays on non-critical tickets.
fr.ch4_tier1_focus_availability_outage: Structural single points of failure capable of halting essential operations or business continuity.
fr.ch4_tier2_focus_availability_outage: Operational vulnerabilities or incomplete redundancies that degrade performance and extend recovery duration (MTTR).
fr.ch4_tier3_focus_availability_outage: Localized non-redundant component failures with bounded operational impact.
fr.p90_callout_plant_p2: In an operational contingency of this scale across dispatch and logistics facilities, local teams transition after 30 to 60 minutes of outage to manual workaround procedures (paper waybills and decentralized weighbridge capture). While this prevents absolute transportation paralysis, it throttles throughput to 35%-45% of nominal capacity, causing transport queues, reconciliation toil, and inventory discrepancy risks. Restoring transactional sync with the corporate ERP and completing audit balancing requires a window of up to {p90_rec_hours_str} hours.

ja.cmmi_level_4_desc: Continuous telemetry monitoring, quantitative control, and predictive operations. Processes are governed by metrics and formal SLAs.

ja.gloss_mcda_crit_extrema: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Extreme]:** Assesses the level of direct dependency that key operational processes have on this domain. Core business operations depend critically on this platform, and an outage would cause immediate disruption of essential services.
ja.gloss_mcda_crit_alta: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - High]:** Reflects high operational dependency, though a brief latency tolerance exists before core business continuity is disrupted.
ja.gloss_mcda_crit_media: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Medium]:** The domain provides supportive or back-office services whose temporary downtime is manageable via standard contingency procedures.
ja.gloss_mcda_reg_critica: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Critical]:** Severe regulatory exposure under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001), where security deficiencies directly incur high statutory penalties and direct corporate liability.
ja.gloss_mcda_reg_moderada: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Moderate]:** Strict corporate compliance and security baseline mandates apply, requiring periodic independent IT control audits.
ja.gloss_mcda_reg_estandar: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Standard]:** Standard operational compliance based on engineering best practices without direct statutory critical scrutiny.
ja.gloss_mcda_viab_fav: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Feasible]:** Transformation feasibility is favorable. Modernization initiatives can be delivered with mature technologies and market resources without critical disruption.
ja.gloss_mcda_viab_comp: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Complex]:** High execution complexity due to structural technical debt, maintenance bottlenecks, or specialized skill scarcity.
ja.gloss_dii_alta: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Stability]:** The extremely low Decision Instability Index mathematically certifies that findings are robust and unaffected by small evidence variations.
ja.gloss_dii_mod: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - Moderate Stability]:** Moderate sensitivity; findings are substantially stable though specific sub-scores depend on evolving architectural interpretation.
ja.gloss_dii_vol: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Sensitivity]:** High volatility; limited evidentiary backing suggests further confirmation is required to lock target maturity scores.
ja.gloss_erc_alta: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - High]:** High structural influence; a critical outage in this domain easily propagates cascades destabilizing connected enterprise systems.
ja.gloss_erc_media: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Medium]:** Moderate structural influence; disruption remains contained, impacting only immediately adjacent workloads.
ja.gloss_erc_baja: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Low/Isolated]:** Low structural influence; failures remain strictly isolated within this technical perimeter without holding-wide impact.
ja.gloss_spof_crit: **Single Point of Failure (SPOF) [YES - Critical]:** This domain represents an unmitigated structural bottleneck without sufficient failover, requiring immediate remediation.
ja.gloss_spof_stable: **Single Point of Failure (SPOF) [NO - Stable]:** This domain does not act as an isolated single point of failure within the overall operational topology.

ja.interdep_intro_text: テクノロジーインフラは孤立して機能しません。特定領域の事象がリスクを伝播し事業継続性に即時影響を及ぼします。そのため本節では技術診断を実際の戦略的影響と結びつけます:

ja.value_hexagon_heading: レジリエンス価値レバー
ja.value_hexagon_intro: 近代化の意思決定を正当化する包括的な事業視点を提供するため、本診断はOpen FAIRのリスク定量化を国際的な**TBM (Technology Business Management)**および**FinOps**フレームワークで補完し、6つの価値レバーで分析します:
value_hexagon_bullets: レバー 1 - 労働資本の回収 (Lean IT): 自動化なら数秒で完了する手動ルーチン作業に浪費される直接的な人件費を定量化。
レバー 2 - 人材の機会費用: 熟練エンジニアが戦略的革新ではなく対症療法的保守に拘束されることによる逸失利益。
レバー 3 - プロジェクト遅延コスト: 手動プロビジョニング待ちによって重要事業施策が遅延することによる間接的損失。
レバー 4 - インフラ浪費の排除: 防御的な過剰サイジングや遊休資産に起因する不要なコストの削減。
レバー 5 - レガシー延長サポート費用の回避: サポート終了製品に対するベンダーの割高な延長保守費用の回避。
レバー 6 - テールリスクからのバランスシート保護: 設定ミスによる致命的障害やNIS2制裁等の極端な損害の防止。

ja.fair_guide_intro: さらに、詳細カードにおける財務的影響の理解を促すため、予測エクスポージャー指標は以下を表します:
fair_guide_bullets: 年間予想損失額 (ALE): 毎年予想される平均経済的コスト。運用の不作為コストの基準値となります。
ワーストケース (CVaR): 最悪の10%のシナリオにおける平均値。深刻な脅威が同時発生した場合の財務的損失規模を示します。
確率的レンジ: 軽微な影響から規制制裁やSLA違反による理論上の最大損失までの統計的スペクトラム。

ja.maturity_scale_intro: 成熟度は1.00から5.00までの分析スケールで評価され、各レベルが統制段階を定義します:
maturity_scale_levels: **Level 1 - Initial (1.00 - 1.59):** Ad-hoc, reactive practices dependent on heroic individual efforts.
**Level 2 - Managed (1.60 - 2.59):** Basic operational processes established at tactical level with inter-silo inconsistencies.
**Level 3 - Defined (2.60 - 3.59):** Formalized and consistently documented processes across the entire enterprise.
**Level 4 - Quantitatively Managed (3.60 - 4.59):** Quantitatively measured capabilities aligned with corporate IT governance.
**Level 5 - Optimized (4.60 - 5.00):** Operational excellence model characterized by high automation and continuous improvement.

ja.appendix_fair_fallacy: 単一推定量が実際のエクスポージャーを歪める「平均値の誤謬」を防ぐため、プラットフォームエンジンは検出された所見ごとに10,000回のモンテカルロ保険数理シミュレーションを実行します:
ja.systemic_resilience_intro: プラットフォーム横断的な回復力を定量化し、単一領域を超えるシステミックな脆弱性を特定するため、多基準意思決定分析 (MCDA) およびネットワーク伝播アルゴリズムを用いて以下の高度な意思決定指標を算出します:
systemic_resilience_indicators_list: 1. **ビジネス重要度 (MCDA) [範囲 0%〜100%]:** 80%を超える値（極めて高い - 重要基盤）は、当該技術領域が中核事業サービスを直接支えていることを示します。
2. **規制圧力 (MCDA) [範囲 0%〜100%]:** 80%を超える値（致命的）は、厳格な法定・規制基準（NIS2指令、DORA、ISO 27001等）の対象であることを示します。
3. **運用の実現可能性 (MCDA) [範囲 0%〜100%]:** 提案されたロードマップ施策の技術的・運用的実現性を測定します。
4. **診断不安定性指数 (DII) [範囲 0%〜100%]:** 収集された証拠データの変動に対する評価の感度と数学的安定性を測定します。
5. **連鎖障害伝播指数 (ERC) [範囲 0.000〜1.000]:** PageRank型ネットワーク中心性アルゴリズムを用い、障害が他領域へ波及する影響度を測定します。
6. **単一障害点 (SPOF) [YES / NO]:** 構造的冗長性の分類。'YES'は重要資産にアクティブな冗長性が欠如していることを警告します。
ja.lm_scale_title: 直接/間接損失規模基準スケール (LM)
ja.systemic_resilience_indicators_title: 高度なシステミック・レジリエンス指標
ja.tef_scale_title: 脅威事象頻度基準スケール (TEF)
ja.appendix_fair_rationale_p: 従来型の定性的リスクマトリクス (高/中/低) は初期分類には有用ですが、投資判断やROIの正当化に必要な保険数理的精度を欠いています。本診断ではOpen FAIR™標準 (ISO/IEC 27005準拠) を採用し、年間財務エクスポージャーを定量的にモデル化します。
ja.appendix_fair_dual_layer_p: 技術的欠陥が企業のバランスシートに波及するプロセスを追跡するため、本モデルは脅威シナリオを一歩ずつ再構成します（「インシデントの経歴」）。保険数理モデルは財務的影響を2つの明確な層に区分します:
ja.appendix_fair_dual_layer_b1: 層1: 脆弱性モデリング (FAIR-CAM™標準) - 防御有効性の確率的校正: 脅威事象の発生から始まり、統制を突破して損失を生じる確率を脆弱性 (_VULN_) として定義します。監査された成熟度に基づき**FAIR-CAM™**を適用し、一次損失（緊急対応および復旧工数）を対数正規分布でモデル化します。
ja.appendix_fair_dual_layer_b2: 層2: 二次エクスポージャーおよびデューデリジェンス (FAIR-MAM™標準) - 条件付き規制エクスポージャー伝播: 一次損失に続き、デューデリジェンスの立証度合いに基づき二次責任が発動します。**FAIR-MAM™**を適用し、{reg_name}の下での制裁金（最大 {reg_fine_limit}）やSLA違反ペナルティをロジスティック曲線でシミュレートします。
ja.appendix_fair_sim_kernel_p: 概念的論理を超えた本診断の中核的差異は、その数学的アーキテクチャにあります。リスクエンジンは、バーゼルIII基準に準拠した2段階複合リスクプロセスに基づく**10,000回のモンテカルロシミュレーション**を実行します:
appendix_fair_sim_bullets: 専門家抽出 (マルチエージェント敵対的合意形成): ベイズ更新を用いて事前分布を校正し、二重計上を防止します。
脅威発生頻度 (負の二項分布): サイバー攻撃の集中発生や過分散を捉えて年間脅威数をシミュレートします。
統制防御 (二項分布プロセス): ロジスティック減衰関数に従い、防御が脅威を阻止するか失敗するかを判定します。
損失深刻度 (ソフト切断付き対数正規分布): 法的上限で切断された裾の重い財務インパクトをモデル化します。
多変量相関 (方向性ガウス・コピュラ): 一次損失と二次規制制裁を因果的に結合する非対称テール依存性を導入します。
ja.appendix_fair_metrics_intro: 10,000回の仮想シミュレーション結果を集約・順位付けし、累積損失分布と投資正当化のための3つの決定打となる指標を算出します:
appendix_fair_metrics_bullets: 年間予想損失額 (ALE - Annual Loss Exposure): 全損失シナリオの算術平均値であり、現状維持における潜在的な平均不作為コストを表します。
期待ショートフォール (CVaR / Expected Shortfall): 損失分布の上位2.5%（最悪ケース）の数学的平均値。テールリスクの真の破壊力を捉えます。
もっともらしい損失レンジ (P10 - P90 区間): 現実的な予算計画のための、通常の年次損失が変動する高信頼区間を定義します。
ja.appendix_c_custody_p1: 重要インフラ監査で要求される不変性、フォレンジックな追跡可能性および厳格性を保証するため、すべての証跡と結論は厳格な管理チェーンの下で収集されています。主な情報源は以下の通りです:
ja.matrix_dim_1_path_a:
• Annualized cost of inaction estimated at **{currency}{formatted_ale_item}**/year (ALE from operational friction and unplanned downtime).
• Latent exposure in a severe crisis or cascading outage scenario reaching up to **{currency}{formatted_p90}** (P90).
• Cumulative technical debt growth and continuous rise in maintenance overhead over a 3- to 5-year horizon.
ja.matrix_dim_1_path_b:
• Progressive amortization of structural technical debt through targeted investment.
• Over **80%** reduction in systemic risk exposure and elimination of single points of failure.
• Defensible ROI grounded in eliminated downtime and reduced manual toil.
ja.matrix_dim_2_path_a:
• Reactive siloed operations heavily dependent on manual firefighting.
• Escalating Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) and reliance on emergency triage.
• Late incident detection reported by end users or business operations.
ja.matrix_dim_2_path_b:
• Unified real-time telemetry with proactive incident prevention prior to service impact.
• Radical MTTR reduction through automated procedures and executable runbooks.
• Service Level Agreements (SLAs) guaranteed by continuous observability.
ja.matrix_dim_3_path_a:
• Structural difficulty demonstrating continuous compliance during internal and external audits.
• Exposure to non-compliance findings and operational contingencies under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, ISO 27001, ISO 22301).
ja.matrix_dim_3_path_b:
• Auditable compliance by design through structured technical governance.
• Minimized non-compliance exposure and automated documentation traceability.
ja.matrix_dim_4_path_a:
• Continuous cognitive overload on IT specialists handling low-value manual toil.
• Engineering fatigue, risk of critical operational knowledge loss, and delayed strategic projects.
ja.matrix_dim_4_path_b:
• Standardization and automation of repetitive tasks, liberating engineering capacity.
• Refocusing technical talent on innovation, business scalability, and strategic growth.
ja.appendix_fair_convergence_note: *(収束性およびグロスリスクに関する注記: 10,000回のシミュレーション反復試行は、中心極限定理の下での完全な数学的収束を保証します。金額は財務的リスク移転前の潜在的グロスエクスポージャーを表し、技術投資の優先順位付けのための経営指標として機能します)。*

ja.coi_section_title: Multi-Year Projection of Cost of Inaction

methodology_three_phases_bullets: **Phase 1: Evidence Ingestion & Operational Verification:** On-site technical inspection, engineering interviews, and network/facility topology validation.
**Phase 2: Topological Dependency Modeling & SPOF Analysis:** Cascading failure propagation analysis mapping facility disruptions to core organizational operations.
**Phase 3: Quantitative Actuarial Simulation (Open FAIR):** 10,000-run Monte Carlo stochastic modeling quantifying annualized financial loss exposure (ALE) and P90 tail risk.
ja.cross_cutting_debt_title: Cross-Cutting Technical Debt Analysis & Structural Risk Patterns
ja.cross_cutting_debt_intro: Beyond vertical pillar baselines, the assessment identifies three horizontal friction patterns spanning the entire infrastructure:
ja.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_1: **1. 継続的なテレメトリの欠如と未監視の電力容量:** 配電盤およびインテリジェントラックPDUにおいてデジタルリアルタイムテレメトリが不足しており、新規負荷展開時の電力マージン把握が困難です。
ja.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_2: **2. Operational Silos Between Facilities (BMS) and Central Enterprise IT Observability:** Electromechanical infrastructure operates decoupled from corporate monitoring. Environmental anomalies fail to trigger correlated early warnings, causing degradations to be discovered only after server cluster outages.
ja.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_3: **3. 非構造化保守手順と作業許可プロセスの摩擦:** 予防保守巡回、発電機切替試験、および外部委託業者の入室管理において、デジタル承認ワークフローと不変の監査証跡が確立されていません。
ja.rore_value_hexagon_title: The Return on Resilience & Efficiency Hexagon (RoRE / TBM & FinOps)
ja.rore_value_hexagon_intro: Infrastructure risk mitigation unlocks direct economic value structured across six strategic levers under the TBM and FinOps frameworks:
rore_value_hexagon_bullets: **1. Labor Capital Recovery (Lean IT):** Eliminating reactive manual rounds and physical clamp measurements, freeing engineering capacity for core innovation initiatives.
**2. Cost of Delay Reduction:** Accelerating capacity provisioning and facilitating seamless post-merger technology onboarding for organizational acquisitions (M&A).

**3. Capacity Optimization & Operational Efficiency:** Eliminating throughput bottlenecks, over-provisioning, and resource waste, reducing operational platform overhead and infrastructure energy consumption by up to 28%.
**4. Extended Support Cost Avoidance:** Phasing out end-of-life (EoL) infrastructure before facing punitive non-warranty vendor maintenance pricing tiers.
**5. Tail-Risk Balance Sheet Mitigation (CVaR):** Insulating operational cash flows against catastrophic multi-day outages threatening commercial revenue and continuous operations.

**6. Regulatory & Governance Compliance Assurance:** Continuous audit-grade telemetry and incident records ensuring alignment with international resilience frameworks and preventing punitive regulatory sanctions.

ch3_intro_archetypes.INFRASTRUCTURE_PHYSICAL: This chapter presents the technical assessment of physical facilities, electromechanical power distribution, and plant networking across {tower_name} at {client_name}. The analysis evaluates infrastructure resilience across three dimensions: power and precision cooling redundancy, single point of failure (SPOF) elimination, and preventive maintenance discipline.
ch3_intro_archetypes.COMPUTE_PLATFORMS: This chapter documents the technical diagnostic of compute platforms, virtualization clusters, and workload execution environments comprising {tower_name} at {client_name}. The assessment examines cluster capacity to sustain continuous transaction throughput, hypervisor memory saturation, and operating system support lifecycles.
ch3_intro_archetypes.SECURITY_GOVERNANCE: This section presents the technical evaluation of persistence mechanisms, access controls, and operational governance across {tower_name} at {client_name}. The analysis verifies data immutability, infrastructure defense resilience, and contingency recovery readiness safeguarding enterprise continuity.

ja.ch3_intro_p1: This chapter executes the technical diagnostic of the technology platform at {client_name}, evaluating the {tower_name} infrastructure across three analytical dimensions: (1) architectural resilience against single points of failure (SPOFs) and redundancy deficits; (2) physical and logical obsolescence relative to vendor support lifecycles; and (3) the maturity of operational runbooks and preventive maintenance regimes. Triangulating these factors under the CMMI framework establishes the operational risk baseline and substantiates modernization priorities.

To avoid the "Flaw of Averages" (where fixed single-point estimates distort true risk), the platform engine executes a 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo actuarial simulation algorithm for every detected finding.

ja.components_evaluated_lead: The technical scope evaluated within this tower encompasses the following key components and subsystems:
ja.default_primary_workloads: mission-critical customer-facing workloads, real-time transaction pipelines, and core enterprise digital services
ja.exec_narrative_p1: Every technological architecture upholds a financial promise. For {tower_name}, that promise currently rests on fragile foundations (Level {score_display} - {global_band}). Our forensic analysis reveals that the underlying infrastructure is not suffering from a lack of capacity, but rather from a silent erosion of operational resilience: structural vulnerabilities where an unpredicted fault holds the potential to sever {client_name}'s business continuity.
ja.exec_narrative_p2: To translate this technical fragility into boardroom economics, we rejected arbitrary industry averages. By applying an actuarial model calibrated against actual exposed corporate turnover ({effective_exposed_revenue_formatted} {currency_code}), we established a composite downtime burn rate of **{hourly_cost}/h** (incorporating a {sector_impact_factor_pct}% direct revenue velocity penalty, SLA breach accruals, and incident labor burden). This valuation directly links the platform's vulnerabilities with {client_name}'s operating cash flow.
ja.exec_narrative_p3: Furthermore, to prevent mathematical inflation, we deduplicated overlapping blast radii via joint failure probability: true net exposure stands at **{ale_hours} critical hours annually**, crystallizing a net Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE) of **{ale_formatted}**. Under a severe tail-risk scenario (90th percentile), an uncontrollable outage could cripple operations for up to {p90_hours} hours, incurring a catastrophic exposure of **{p90_formatted}**.
ja.exec_narrative_p4: Deferring remediation is not cost containment; it is the unhedged underwriting of an operational catastrophe. Executing the proposed target roadmap eliminates the current operational paralysis and automates resilience in {tower_name}. This capital allocation converts an unpredictable technical liability into hardened operational equity, safeguarding both {client_name}'s EBITDA and institutional trust against severe disruption.

ja.p90_callout_body_template: Consistent with the Chapter 1 executive synthesis, actuarial modeling at the 90th percentile (P90) evaluates a compound failure triggered by {compound_failure_trigger}. Under this asymptotic stress regime, the physical reconstruction, state synchronization, and operational verification window extends up to {p90_recovery_hours} hours. The projected maximum contingent financial exposure reaches {p90_total_contingency}, comprising {direct_stoppage_loss} in direct operational stoppage losses and {secondary_disaster_spend} in secondary disaster expenditures (emergency OEM vendor escalation, expedited hardware logistics, and Tier-3 specialized triage).
ja.p90_callout_p1: To evaluate the practical resilience limit of this capability tower, the model simulates a severe, plausible scenario in which multiple critical failures occur simultaneously ({compound_failure_trigger}). Unlike routine isolated incidents, this case examines the operational reality when both primary systems and their backup mechanisms fail concurrently.
ja.p90_callout_p2: In a disruption of this magnitude, recovery requires more than restarting equipment; teams must rebuild operations step by step and verify that no critical business data has been corrupted. Under current technical conditions, fully restoring service and validating data consistency would require up to {p90_recovery_hours} hours.
ja.p90_callout_p3: The total financial exposure of this scenario reaches {p90_total_contingency}. This impact breaks down clearly into two categories: {direct_stoppage_loss} in direct losses from halted commercial and operational activity during the outage, and {secondary_disaster_spend} in extraordinary emergency expenses (such as urgent third-party specialist intervention, priority vendor support, and expedited operational recovery services).

ja.sec4_1_alpha_reconciliation: Downtime Cost Scaling by Failure Scope: The baseline corporate rate ({base_rate}/h) represents a complete shutdown of all business operations. Because most technical incidents do not halt 100% of the company, the model scales the hourly cost according to the actual scope of each failure: 70% ({rate_70}/h) for core critical platforms, 40% ({rate_40}/h) for intermediate systems with partial degradation, and 20% ({rate_20}/h) for isolated peripheral components. This ensures each risk card realistically reflects the financial impact of its specific domain.
ja.sle_derivation_formula_bullet: • **Exact Financial Derivation (SLE):** {effective_hours}h operational disruption at {hourly_rate}/hr ({alpha_pct}% operational impact factor over baseline downtime cost of {base_rate}/hr) = {sle_formatted}.

ja.tomo_ch1_lead_in: The transversal audit highlights four critical risk factors requiring immediate leadership action:
ja.tomo_ch1_p1: {client}のテクノロジーポートフォリオに関する包括的評価は{domain_count}の運用ドメインを対象とし、総合成熟度指数は5.00満点中{score}（{cmmi_label}）となりました。このプロファイルは、主要資産において確立された運用能力を備えている一方で、優先的なエグゼクティブガバナンスを必要とする構造的非対称性と集中した財務リスクに晒されているアーキテクチャを反映しています。
ja.tomo_ch1_p3:
国際標準 Open FAIR™（Factor Analysis of Information Risk）に基づく定量的財務リスクモデルは、経営陣の意思決定のために3つの補完的な財務次元を提示します：

1. **年間平均予想損失（ALE）年間換算 {formatted_ale}：** 定常的な運用摩擦、計画外のサポート時間外労働、および損益計算書で吸収される保守債務の年間平均予想損失を反映します。

2. **単一重大インシデント最大損失額（最大 {worst_incident_cost}）：** 最もリスク露出度の高いドメイン（{worst_incident_code} - {worst_incident_domain}）における孤立したコンポーネント障害またはプラットフォーム停止時の直接的な業務影響額を表します。

3. **年間累積危機シナリオ {formatted_p90}：** 厳しい会計年度内に複数の異なるプラットフォームで重大なインシデントが連鎖した場合の集計財務エクスポージャーをモデル化します。

この算定により、経営陣は投下資本単位あたり最大の危機緩和リターンが得られる領域へ近代化投資を的確に配分することができます。
ja.tomo_ch2_footnote: *Methodological note: The consolidated index of {global_score} out of 5.00 reflects the weighted average by operational criticality across domains (the simple arithmetic mean is {simple_mean}).*
ja.tomo_ch2_intro: 技術成熟度評価は、現在のアーキテクチャが業務継続性を維持し、産業プロセスを拡張し、中断リスクを軽減するための実際の能力を判定します。分析モデルは、組織のインフラストラクチャ、アプリケーション、および運用プロセス全体で収集された実証的証拠のみに基づき、1.00から5.00までの標準CMMI（能力成熟度モデル統合）スケールで10の技術タワーを監査します。
ja.tomo_ch2_summary: The CMMI diagnostic places {client_name} at a consolidated index of {global_score} out of 5.00 ({maturity_tier_label}), reflecting an operational foundation with established baseline capabilities alongside inter-domain disparities. Technology domains with the largest deficits against sector benchmarks require targeted modernization roadmaps to mitigate technical debt.
ja.tomo_ch3_financial_hierarchy_body:
To ensure complete transparency for the CFO and Executive Board, the model defines three complementary financial metrics:
1. **Expected Annual Loss Exposure (ALE P50):** Modeled annual operational loss exposure across all evaluated technology domains in the current state.
2. **Single Major Outage Impact (P90 Local):** Maximum loss under an unredundant technical outage halting operations across primary facilities during {duration_str} of downtime and transactional verification.
3. **Annual Aggregate Severe Portfolio Risk (P90 Annual):** The 90th percentile aggregate portfolio loss under compounding adverse operational events across all operating units.
ja.tomo_ch3_financial_hierarchy_title: Actuarial Reconciliation Framework & Metric Hierarchy (Open FAIR™)
ja.tomo_ch3_intro: To eliminate the ambiguity of subjective RAG matrices, this assessment executes the Open FAIR™ standard driven by 10,000-run Monte Carlo stochastic engines, independently evaluating Loss Event Frequency (LEF / TEF) and Loss Magnitude (SLE / LM) across structural failure vectors.
ja.tomo_ch3_p90_1: セクション3.3で詳述した各リスクカードは個別重大インシデントの影響を評価する一方、モンテカルロ確率モデルはポートフォリオ全体における年間の累積テールリスクをシミュレーションしています。
ja.tomo_ch3_p90_2: Under an unfavorable operational year where multiple moderate and severe incidents materialize concurrently across the ten technology domains during the same budget cycle, annual aggregate portfolio losses reach {formatted_p90} at the 90th percentile (Annual P90).
ja.tomo_ch3_p90_3: This {formatted_p90} figure establishes the unprovisioned annual exposure ceiling that fully justifies the strategic technical standardization and contingency investments detailed in the target roadmap.
ja.tomo_ch3_p90_title: 3.4. 最大累積危機シナリオ (P90)
ja.tomo_ch3_rate: The composite hourly downtime baseline is calibrated at **{baseline_rate}**, reconciling operational loss of velocity, contractual SLA penalties, and emergency recovery burden. At operational facilities and primary delivery sites, the local hourly rate reflects the direct interruption of business transaction throughput.

ja.tomo_ch3_tier2_desc: Absence of environmental IoT telemetry, manual change management, and multi-vendor contract duplication.
ja.tomo_ch3_tier3_desc: Non-standardized patch updates and lack of self-service catalog.

ja.tomo_ch4_t10_title: 4.10. 重要出荷システムおよびローカルインフラ（T10）
ja.tomo_ch4_t1_text: Primary technical facilities provide continuous operational support for enterprise compute and connectivity workloads. Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems and diesel backup generators maintain regular preventive maintenance, operating within conventional thermal profiles that require continuous environmental telemetry.
ja.tomo_ch4_t2_text: Core compute environments rely on virtualized platforms experiencing high memory utilization, constraining automated failover headroom during physical node maintenance windows. The platform requires a structured modernization roadmap to align hypervisor licensing with organizational growth.
ja.tomo_ch4_t3_text: The enterprise network fabric interconnects corporate headquarters, regional offices, and operational sites. Core inter-site communications leverage dedicated redundant connectivity, while distributed facilities utilize managed WAN links over secure tunnels, representing a strategic opportunity for SD-WAN convergence.
ja.tomo_ch4_t4_text: Core enterprise storage relies on Almacenamiento Centralizado FAS/AFF arrays via NFS and Fibre Channel. While operational maturity is high (CMMI Level 3), missing WORM SnapLock immutability leaves backup repositories exposed to ransomware encryption. Controller multipathing requires validation to prevent I/O bottlenecks during firmware updates.
ja.tomo_ch4_t5_text: Business continuity and disaster recovery procedures maintain secondary replications of critical data repositories, with full operational resilience requiring automated switchover testing to minimize recovery time objectives (RTO).
ja.tomo_ch4_t6_text: Perimeter security enforces firewall filtering across major ingress points. Identity governance requires federating disparate directory forests into a unified model, deploying Privileged Access Management (PAM) for administrative accounts, and deepening network segmentation.
ja.tomo_ch4_t7_text: Transactional core runs on Oracle Database and SQL Server engines with concentrated administration knowledge. The ITSM platform lacks an automated CMDB federated with the infrastructure digital twin.
ja.tomo_ch4_t8_text: Core ERP platforms and business application suites constitute the operational heart of the enterprise. Cloud workloads and SaaS software subscriptions require unified cost-allocation tagging to optimize recurring spend and eliminate licensing overlap.
ja.tomo_ch4_t8_title: 4.8. Enterprise Applications and Cloud Cost Governance (T8)
ja.tomo_ch4_t9_text: Digital workplace platforms provide standardized productivity and collaboration suites across cloud endpoints, requiring unified mobile device management policies across all distributed offices.

tomo_nexus_catalog.mechanism: Hypervisors and management consoles rely on the general enterprise directory without Tier-0 privileged account isolation.
tomo_nexus_catalog.impact: A security incident on standard user accounts can laterally propagate to core virtualization management.

tomo_nexus_catalog.mechanism: Open airflow distribution without contained hot/cold aisles creates hotspots in high-density compute racks.
tomo_nexus_catalog.impact: Thermal degradation of physical hardware components can trigger unplanned host shutdowns.

tomo_nexus_catalog.mechanism: Secondary backup repositories reside on the same storage fabric as primary production volumes without air-gap.
tomo_nexus_catalog.impact: A catastrophic storage control-plane fault or ransomware sweep threatens backup availability.

tomo_nexus_catalog.mechanism: Core transactional terminals validate settlement records against central enterprise systems across single-homed network tunnels.
tomo_nexus_catalog.impact: A transient local network disruption immediately halts physical truck dispatching at the affected facility.
