tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Single-phase power feed from a single panel without 2N redundancy.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Immediate shutdown of auxiliary electronics and management plane outage.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Point-to-point 10Gb DCI link between sites without redundant ring topology.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Write lock on transactional virtual machines and storage split-brain.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Compressor failure on uncontained high-density perimeter cooling unit.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Thermal server trip within 18 minutes due to hot-air recirculation.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing Tier-0 PAM bastion and brittle directory synchronization across entities.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Identity plane freeze and plant-level ERP authentication lockout.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing WORM immutability and lack of an isolated Cyber Recovery Vault.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Irreversible backup encryption or purge during enterprise ransomware outbreak.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Fibre Channel I/O paths without active multipathing across controllers.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Transactional storage freeze during firmware maintenance reboots.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: IPSec tunnels over commodity internet without dynamic SD-WAN failover.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Telemetry loss to operational dispatch systems stalling industrial product dispatch.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Core database instances without synchronous high-availability cross-site replicas.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Potential data loss and manual recovery with RTO exceeding 8 hours.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: Missing mandatory cost-center tagging policies across public cloud tenants.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Undetected budget drift and recurring licensing overlap.

tomo_spof_catalog.mechanism: End-of-life hardware and unsupported operating systems operating near failure.
tomo_spof_catalog.impact: Total plant scale shutdown with direct downtime losses of impacto operacional significativo.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Disruption of Core Transactional Processing Platforms
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Dispatch PC operating in single-phase non-redundant architecture.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Halted operational transaction processing at a burn rate of impacto operacional significativor.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Deployment of redundant industrial IPC ring with scale hardware bypass.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Excessive Recovery Time from Physical Tape Restores
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Restore procedures depend on physical transport of LTO magnetic tapes.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Effective RTO exceeding 18 hours during major data corruption events.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Implementation of immutable WORM storage tier and cloud replication.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Compute Saturation & upcoming renewal cycles Contract Renewal Shock
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: RAM utilization continuously exceeding 90% and VMware EoL milestones.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Expansion deadlock and steep price escalation during license renewals.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Migration to next-generation sovereign hyperconverged platform.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Thermal Recirculation Across Primary Compute Racks
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Lack of hot/cold aisle containment in primary technical datacenter.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Accelerated CPU component aging and risk of thermal shutdown.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Installation of physical cold-aisle containment and BMS IoT sensors.

tomo_top_risks_catalog.title: Identity Perimeter Disjointedness & NIS2 Compliance Lag
tomo_top_risks_catalog.vuln: Shared privileged administrative accounts and disjointed filiales internacionales forests.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.impact: Credential compromise risk and regulatory compliance exposure.
tomo_top_risks_catalog.mitig: Identity forest consolidation, PAM deployment, and mandatory MFA.

T1.inventory: 2 technical rooms at primary headquarters, generator sets in ring topology, N+1 UPS schemes, gas fire suppression, and perimeter HVAC.
findings: Absence of hot/cold aisle aerodynamic containment causing thermal recirculation across compute racks at ASHRAE limits.
Lack of real-time IoT power telemetry on electrical panels and PDUs, preventing phase-level capacity measurement.
Absence of biometric access controls at airlocks and electronic work permits (ePtW) required for NIS2 compliance.
Lack of automated correlation between environmental sensors and fire suppression systems for adjacent containment.
Electromechanical preventive maintenance managed reactively without centralized CMMS or live-load transfer testing.
strengths: Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems in N+1 redundancy with certified preventive maintenance routines.
Precision air conditioning units (CRAC) providing environmental control across technical datacenter rooms.
Automated clean-agent fire suppression and detection deployed in primary technical spaces.
Optical and thermal fire detection zoning under raised floors and ceilings complying with engineering standards.
Monitored electrical distribution switchboards and technical alarms integrated into operations control.

T2.inventory: 3 hyperconverged nodes running legacy VMware ESXi and Windows/Linux server workloads with mixed cloud instances.
findings: Structural CPU and memory saturation (>90%) preventing N+1 failover between technical rooms without workload degradation.
Absence of a unified corporate managed Kubernetes platform with security guardrails and service mesh.
Fragmented public cloud adoption lacking automated Landing Zone governance and policy enforcement guardrails.
Absence of declarative Infrastructure as Code (IaC) pipelines for continuous provisioning and version tracking.
Absence of Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) telemetry linked to core business flows.
strengths: Centralized hyperconverged compute cluster delivering dense processing capacity for corporate workloads.
Standardized operating system base templates and container execution environments for microservices.
Production hosting of mission-critical workloads (SAP S/4HANA) on Tier-1 enterprise hyperscalers (GCP/Azure).
Automated virtual server cloning and baseline deployment procedures across primary clusters.
Hypervisor-level automated high availability (HA) failover operational across compute nodes.

T3.inventory: Dual-core switching infrastructure, perimeter firewalls, and SD-WAN links interconnecting 18 operating country sites.
findings: Access layer switches across remote quarries and industrial plants approaching commercial End-of-Life (EoL).
Secondary plant interconnects dependent on static IPSec tunnels lacking dynamic traffic steering and SD-WAN failover.
Point-to-point Data Center Interconnect (DCI) lacking physical ring topology and exterior conduit diversification.
Cloud interconnect architecture lacking centralized transit routing (Cloud Router) and automated multi-region failover.
Manual network administration via CLI without declarative NetDevOps workflows or version-controlled configurations.
strengths: Dual-core backbone switching infrastructure with redundant uplinks across technical distribution frames.
Corporate WAN and SD-WAN connectivity established across manufacturing plants, quarries, and branch offices.
Dedicated high-speed 10 Gbps point-to-point fiber interconnecting primary operational datacenters.
High-performance direct interconnect ports linking core routing to public cloud transit hubs.
Centralized bandwidth monitoring probes and active link telemetry supervised in network consoles.

T4.inventory: Enterprise SAN arrays and NAS clusters replicating asynchronously across dual technical rooms.
findings: Lack of native Calidad de Servicio (QoS) bandwidth shaping on SAN arrays, exposing critical databases to I/O noisy neighbors.
Fragmented audit logging on storage controllers without dedicated write-once-read-many (WORM) audit vaults.
Reliance on local snapshot copies without physical cyber isolation against targeted ransomware encryption campaigns.
Absence of strict WORM immutability (SnapLock) activation across mission-critical volume snapshots for NIS2 compliance.
Operational friction and blurred boundary delineation in storage administration between internal IT and external support.
subpillars: Security & Access Controls for Data Platforms
strengths: High-performance enterprise storage arrays featuring dynamic capacity allocation and thin-provisioning.
Storage capacity thresholds monitored with proactive alert notifications in central dashboards.
Scheduled snapshot policies and asynchronous block-level replication between active datacenters.
Protected enterprise storage volumes configured with accidental deletion safeguards and data-at-rest encryption.
Native SAN storage volume integration supporting corporate hypervisor clusters.

T5.inventory: Tape-based and disk backup targets with manual disaster recovery playbooks and scheduled off-site replication.
findings: Concentration of datacenter resilience within a shared geographic perimeter, creating a geographic Single Point of Failure.
Technical recovery times (RTO > 4 hours) exceeding operational tolerance thresholds for continuous core transaction processing.
Absence of scheduled, full-scale disaster recovery exercises (game days) under live production mains power disconnection.
Absence of an isolated Cyber Recovery Vault with automated forensic data validation prior to mass restore execution.
Lack of symmetric standby capacity across twin datacenters preventing transparent workload failover without shutdown.
strengths: Documented contingency and disaster recovery operational procedures for essential industrial systems.
Scheduled disk and tape backup policies with verified off-site custody procedures.
Skilled internal engineering team possessing deep operational experience in manual plant system restoration.
Air-gapped offline magnetic tape backups maintained in physically isolated custody facilities.
Local electromechanical component redundancy and automated core server service failover.

T6.inventory: Centralized Active Directory domains, endpoint EDR agents, and outsourced SOC monitoring alerts.
findings: Identity plane fragmentation and persistence of over-privileged static administrative credentials lacking dynamic JIT elevation.
Absence of an enterprise Privileged Access Management (PAM) vault enforcing automated credential rotation and session monitoring.
Infrequent security configuration baseline audits lacking automated configuration drift detection across systems.
Partial vulnerability scanning coverage omitting legacy virtual machines, industrial gateways, and acquired subsidiaries.
Flat industrial plant network topology lacking East-West microsegmentation, allowing undetected threat propagation.
strengths: Centralized enterprise identity and access management directory (Active Directory).
Enforced corporate password complexity policies and initial administrative role segregation.
Homogeneous endpoint detection and response (EDR) agent deployment with external SOC monitoring.
Scheduled external perimeter penetration scanning and corporate operating system update cycles.
Next-generation perimeter firewalls enforcing corporate network traffic filtering and secure VPN.

T7.inventory: Relational database clusters (SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL) and central ITSM ticketing platform.
findings: Misalignment between technical infrastructure SLAs and core manufacturing operations, obscuring plant-level outage impact.
Manual incident triage and dispatch workflows lacking intelligent routing based on industrial operational criticality.
Absence of an automated, federated Configuration Management Database (CMDB) maintaining live dependency maps.
Reactive root cause analysis (RCA) procedures lacking institutionalized Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) error budgets.
Fragmented monitoring tooling lacking cross-domain causal event correlation between on-premise, cloud, and OT environments.
strengths: Documented IT service catalog and service level agreements (SLAs) established for internal business units.
Centralized IT Service Management (ITSM) ticketing platform structuring operational incidents and requests.
Centralized hardware and software license inventory maintained by the IT infrastructure department.
Structured post-incident reviews conducted following major service outages to identify direct causes.
Core infrastructure telemetry probes (CPU, memory, storage, ping) transmitting alerts to central consoles.

T8.inventory: ERP applications (SAP), logistics management platforms, and multi-cloud SaaS subscriptions.
findings: Critical architectural obsolescence across legacy operating systems and database engines lacking budgeted modernization paths.
Asymmetric governance between corporate headquarters and newly acquired subsidiaries, perpetuating operational silos.
Absence of continuous, quantified technical risk governance modeled under Open FAIR standards.
Reactive cloud financial governance lacking automated resource tagging enforcement and showback/chargeback models.
Absence of executive dashboards correlating technology investments with measurable plant productivity gains.
subpillars: Value Realization, Executive Metrics & Continuous Improvement
strengths: Strategic technology roadmap aligned with corporate business growth and digital modernization goals.
Periodic IT governance committee and structured capital expenditure approval processes.
Formal corporate information security policies and accounting/tax compliance oversight.
Centralized monthly billing visibility within multi-cloud consoles (GCP, Azure, and OCI).
Consolidated IT operational expenditure metrics tracked for senior financial leadership.

T9.inventory: Managed Windows 11 and macOS corporate endpoints, Microsoft 365 productivity suite, and mobile MDM profiles.
findings: Plant and quarry endpoint devices administered locally without centralized modern device management enrollment.
Vulnerability across shared industrial plant workstations lacking passwordless biometric or FIDO2 authentication.
Document sprawl across unmanaged cloud repositories lacking automated lifecycle and data retention governance policies.
Manual endpoint provisioning and workstation support processes increasing fulfillment lead times across remote facilities.
Absence of Digital Employee Experience (DEX) real-time telemetry for proactive degradation and latency detection.
subpillars: Productividad, Colaboración y Gestión del Conocimiento
strengths: Standardized corporate endpoint fleet operating under unified modern management baselines.
Secure remote connectivity and multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled for knowledge workers.
Cloud collaboration and productivity suites (M365) widely adopted across business units.
Structured Level-1 service desk and automated operating system security patch distribution.
Direct communication channels and periodic user satisfaction surveys conducted by the IT team.

T10.inventory: Mission-critical core processing engines, enterprise clearing interfaces, and operational transactional platforms.
findings: Core transactional terminals and processing engines operating on outdated hardware configurations and legacy operating systems.
Software modifications on legacy transactional components applied manually without version control in Git repositories.
Batch processing queues and data transfers concentrated in peak operating windows causing storage controller I/O spikes.
Direct database-level point-to-point links between legacy and modern systems lacking governed API contracts.
Critical dependence on tacit operational knowledge held by specialized personnel approaching retirement on legacy stacks.
strengths: Core transactional processing engines maintained with verified operational stability and scheduled maintenance.
Robust, well-rehearsed manual dispatch continuity procedures during communication disruptions.
Automated transactional synchronization interfaces transferring event logs and clearing records to central enterprise ERP.
Functional point-to-point integration connectors guaranteeing dispatch and billing continuity.
Dedicated and highly qualified on-site operational staff ensuring resilient local execution.

ja.tomo_triad_bottleneck_desc: Operational reliance on manual interventions by internal engineering teams and facility vulnerability during network degradation.
ja.tomo_triad_gap_desc: High resource pressure across core clusters (>90%), baseline operational telemetry, and upcoming software contract renewals requiring strategic consolidation.
ja.tomo_triad_strength_desc: Robust mechanical fire suppression across technical facilities alongside centralized structured storage.

T1.operational_mission: physical data center facilities, electrical continuity, and precision climate control
T1.dilemma_anchor: When evaluating electromechanical resilience and physical facility redundancy,
T1.posture_modernization_focus: reinforcing electromechanical redundancy and precision cooling to safeguard uninterrupted power to core systems

T2.operational_mission: physical and virtual compute platforms, hypervisors, and hybrid cloud workloads
T2.dilemma_anchor: From a platform engineering and compute capacity standpoint,
T2.posture_modernization_focus: expanding cluster compute elasticity and ensuring automated workload failover without performance degradation

T3.operational_mission: enterprise networks, software-defined WAN, campus switching, and inter-site transit connectivity
T3.dilemma_anchor: When evaluating network transport topology and data communications resilience,
T3.posture_modernization_focus: embedding active path redundancy across transit links and enforcing automated software-defined traffic routing

T4.operational_mission: enterprise storage architecture, SAN/NAS arrays, persistent volume fabrics, and backup repositories
T4.dilemma_anchor: From a persistent storage architecture and data tiering perspective,
T4.posture_modernization_focus: guaranteeing storage throughput and eliminating I/O bottlenecks across mission-critical persistent volumes

T5.operational_mission: business continuity architectures, high-availability clusters, backup registries, and disaster recovery procedures
T5.dilemma_anchor: When assessing organizational survivability, disaster recovery orchestration, and cyber recovery readiness,
T5.posture_modernization_focus: tightening automated failover thresholds (RTO/RPO) and validating immutable cyber recovery procedures against systemic disruption

T6.operational_mission: cybersecurity architecture, zero trust identity governance, privileged access management, and threat defense
T6.dilemma_anchor: From an enterprise cybersecurity, perimeter defense, and identity protection standpoint,
T6.posture_modernization_focus: elevating privileged access governance, enforcing hardware-backed multi-factor authentication, and deploying continuous threat monitoring

T7.operational_mission: IT service management (ITSM), incident command, change governance, and operational support workflows
T7.dilemma_anchor: When reviewing operational service delivery, incident response cadences, and ITIL process maturity,
T7.posture_modernization_focus: streamlining incident triage automation, enforcing change management rigor, and reducing mean time to repair (MTTR)

T8.operational_mission: technology strategy, enterprise IT governance, portfolio prioritization, and cloud financial operations (FinOps)
T8.dilemma_anchor: From an enterprise technology governance, architectural review, and cloud financial optimization standpoint,
T8.posture_modernization_focus: enforcing automated cloud expenditure guardrails, optimizing unit economics, and aligning architectural roadmaps with business OKRs

T9.operational_mission: digital workplace engineering, unified endpoint management, collaboration tooling, and end-user support
T9.dilemma_anchor: When evaluating user computing environments, endpoint security posture, and workplace productivity tools,
T9.posture_modernization_focus: standardizing endpoint device configurations, enforcing device health compliance, and automating workstation provisioning

T10.operational_mission: core transactional processing engines, legacy applications, payment and settlement rails, and high-throughput clearing interfaces
T10.dilemma_anchor: When auditing core mission-critical platforms, high-throughput transaction processing, and legacy application resilience,
T10.posture_modernization_focus: modernizing legacy transactional dependencies, decoupling batch windows, and establishing resilient API integrations

DEFAULT.operational_mission: supporting essential operational capabilities with standardized architectural baselines
DEFAULT.dilemma_anchor: When reviewing baseline operational capabilities and architectural alignment,
DEFAULT.posture_modernization_focus: reinforcing operational controls and modernizing key infrastructure dependencies

ja.tomo_ch2_benchmark_methodology_body: 本診断で採用されているベンチマークは、重工業および建築資材セクターの実証的中央値（P50）を反映しており、標準化されたITインフラ領域と長期償却サイクルを伴う工場OT環境との間の構造的な非対称性をモデル化しています。
ja.tomo_ch2_benchmark_methodology_title: 業界ベンチマーク調整方法論（中央値 P50）
ja.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_1: • Out-of-Contract 24x7 OEM Emergency Engineering Intervention ({bucket_1_cost} — {bucket_1_pct} of emergency spend): Reactive engagement of Tier-3 Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specialists at emergency Time & Materials rates outside standard SLAs to rebuild hypervisors, storage arrays, or network switches whose standard support has lapsed.
ja.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_2: • Urgent Spot-Market Hardware Procurement and Dedicated Courier Logistics ({bucket_2_cost} — {bucket_2_pct} of emergency spend): Immediate spot-market purchase of replacement servers, controllers, drives, or switches at premium availability pricing, combined with dedicated same-day air/ground courier transport directly to affected facilities.
ja.tomo_ch3_emergency_bucket_3: • Specialized Database Recovery and Level-3 Forensic Triage Services ({bucket_3_cost} — {bucket_3_pct} of emergency spend): Engagement of external recovery engineers specialized in repairing corrupted transactional tables (core ERP/corporate databases), reconciling in-flight transactions interrupted by the crash, and performing forensic containment prior to production restart.
ja.tomo_ch3_exec_intro_p1: 本章では、国際標準であるOpen FAIR™に基づき、現行アーキテクチャの財務的影響および運用リスクを定量化します。その目的は、現在のITインフラを運用する実際の実質コストに関して、IT部門および経営委員会に対して客観的かつ財務的に立証可能な基盤を提供することにあります。本モデルは確率と深刻度に基づいて主要な技術障害シナリオを特定・優先順位付けし、日常業務において損益計算書が吸収している継続的損失と、重大なインシデントや複合危機発生時に企業が直面する直接的な損失規模を測定します。

ja.tomo_ch2_summary_p1: 統合されたグローバル成熟度指数は5.00満点中{overall_maturity}であり、技術プラットフォームはレベル2（反復可能）に位置しています。この結果は、明確に分化した2つの速度を持つアーキテクチャを反映しています。一方では、企業の基盤機能であるストレージとバックアップ（3.30）およびデジタルワークプレイス（3.10）がレベル3（定義済み）に到達しており、文書化された標準、集中型アーキテクチャ、および予測可能なサービスレベルの下で運用されています。
ja.tomo_ch2_summary_p2: 他方、産業およびトランザクションの実行を支える領域—事業継続性（2.10）、業務アプリケーション（2.40）、および出荷システム（2.40）—は、レベル2の事後対応的な領域に留まっています。これらの領域では、運用の安定性は技術スタッフの事後対応的な尽力、自動冗長性を欠いたローカル構成、およびポイントツーポイントの統合に依存しています。この構造的な非対称性は、第3章で分析される運用上および財務上の主要なリスク要因となっています。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T1: 堅牢な設備を備えたデータセンターだが、熱的分離と基本的な電力テレメトリに制約が存在。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T2: Stable core virtualization and hyperconverged platforms, constrained by high memory pressure and upcoming technological refresh milestones.
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T3: 稼働中のWAN/SD-WANトポロジだが、IT/OTセグメンテーションの強化と主要採石場での二重回線化が必要。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T4: 正式な保持ポリシーとローカルレプリケーションを備えた、中央集権的で予測可能なストレージおよびバックアップ構成。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T5: 工場環境における非公式なDRP手順、手動介入への高い依存、および長期化する復旧時間。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T6: 有効な境界セキュリティ制御だが、OTネットワークの可視性向上と特権アクセス管理（PAM）の導入が必要。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T7: 安定したトランザクションデータベース運用だが、パッチ適用の自動化とITSMガバナンスの標準化が未完了。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T8: 財務領域で統合されたSAP/ERPエコシステムだが、手動の連携処理と分断されたライセンス契約が課題。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T9: Microsoft 365の下で標準化されたデジタルワークプレイス環境であり、オフィス環境全体で成熟したガバナンスを確立。
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_T10: Local operations and distributed facility support with operational continuity processes reliant on manual procedures.
ja.tomo_ch2_driver_summary: 標準化されたコーポレートITサービス（レベル3）と脆弱な工場現場運用（レベル2）の間の構造的非対称性。

ja.gloss_erc_high: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - High]:** High structural influence; a critical outage in this domain easily propagates cascades destabilizing connected enterprise systems.
ja.gloss_erc_medium: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Medium]:** Moderate structural influence; disruption remains contained, impacting only immediately adjacent workloads.
ja.gloss_erc_low: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Low/Isolated]:** Low structural influence; failures remain strictly isolated within this technical perimeter without holding-wide impact.
ja.gloss_mcda_crit_extreme: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Extreme]:** Assesses the level of direct dependency that key operational processes have on this domain. Core business operations depend critically on this platform, and an outage would cause immediate disruption of essential services.
ja.gloss_mcda_crit_high: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - High]:** Reflects high operational dependency, though a brief latency tolerance exists before core business continuity is disrupted.
ja.gloss_mcda_crit_medium: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Medium]:** The domain provides supportive or back-office services whose temporary downtime is manageable via standard contingency procedures.
ja.gloss_mcda_reg_critical: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Critical]:** Severe regulatory exposure under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001), where security deficiencies directly incur high statutory penalties and direct corporate liability.
ja.gloss_mcda_reg_moderate: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Moderate]:** Strict corporate compliance and security baseline mandates apply, requiring periodic independent IT control audits.
ja.gloss_mcda_reg_standard: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Standard]:** Standard operational compliance based on engineering best practices without direct statutory critical scrutiny.
ja.gloss_mcda_viab_favorable: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Feasible]:** Transformation feasibility is favorable. Modernization initiatives can be delivered with mature technologies and market resources without critical disruption.
ja.gloss_mcda_viab_complex: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Complex]:** High execution complexity due to structural technical debt, maintenance bottlenecks, or specialized skill scarcity.
ja.gloss_dii_high: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Stability]:** The extremely low Decision Instability Index mathematically certifies that findings are robust and unaffected by small evidence variations.
ja.gloss_dii_moderate: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - Moderate Stability]:** Moderate sensitivity; findings are substantially stable though specific sub-scores depend on evolving architectural interpretation.
ja.gloss_dii_volatile: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Sensitivity]:** High volatility; limited evidentiary backing suggests further confirmation is required to lock target maturity scores.

ja.diag_rationale_divergence_gap: 組織の初期自己評価は5.0満点中{dec_fmt}と予測されていました。しかし、技術的検証およびフォレンジック証拠により{finding_clause}が確認されました。したがって、監査では運用成熟度を客観的に{score_fmt}（{band_label}）に調整し、第2巻における近代化の優先順位を論理づけます。
ja.diag_rationale_divergence_conservative: 観察された技術運用は申告された自己評価（{dec_fmt}）を上回り、能力は{score_fmt}（{band_label}）に調整されました。環境は安定して運用されていますが、{finding_clause}が特定され、次のレベルへの改善余地が示されています。
ja.diag_rationale_divergence_aligned: 初期自己評価（{dec_fmt}）と技術診断は、能力を{score_fmt}（{band_label}）に位置付けることで完全に一致しています。設置基盤は日常の運用を支えていますが、ドメインの回復力は{finding_clause}によって制約されています。
ja.diag_rationale_fact_first_low: この能力の管理は初期段階にあります（5.0点中{score_fmt} - {band_label}）。運用は{finding_clause}によって制約されており、第2巻での標準化が求められます。
ja.diag_rationale_fact_first_mid: この能力は日常的に安定して運用されています（5.0点中{score_fmt} - {band_label}）。ただし、拡張性は{finding_clause}によって制限されています。
ja.diag_rationale_fact_first_high: この能力は確立された成熟度を示しています（5.0点中{score_fmt} - {band_label}）。継続的改善の機会として{finding_clause}が特定されます。

ch3_intro_by_tower.T1: The evaluation of the {tower_title} domain across {client_name} examines electromechanical resilience, physical capacity, and critical facilities stability. This chapter documents the technical diagnosis of computer rooms and processing facilities, auditing uninterrupted power continuity, environmental cooling controls, and preventative maintenance governance over core operational assets.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T2: This chapter documents the architectural assessment of compute platforms, virtualization hypervisors, and hybrid execution environments comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The diagnosis examines cluster sizing and bin-packing capacity, CPU and memory contention, and guest operating system lifecycle management against modern decoupling paradigms.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T3: This chapter analyzes communications architecture, campus networks, and wide-area interconnection links comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The audit evaluates topological resilience against transport failures, microsegmentation and perimeter controls across trust boundaries, and latency stability across corporate services and distributed operating sites.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T4: This chapter addresses the technical diagnosis of enterprise storage platforms, primary arrays, and secondary backup repositories comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation audits database performance and latency SLA compliance, immutable ransomware protection and air-gapping defenses, and storage lifecycle capacity governance.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T5: This chapter examines the operational resilience and disaster recovery posture (BC/DR) governing {tower_title} across {client_name}. The analysis contrasts technical failover and recovery procedures against business disruption tolerances, evaluating physical facility independence, core data protection, and site operational autonomy during central outages.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T6: This section presents the evaluation of the cybersecurity posture, identity governance, and infrastructure defenses comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The diagnostic audits privileged access controls (PAM), threat detection and telemetry visibility, system hardening, and compliance with enterprise security and regulatory frameworks.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T7: This chapter evaluates service delivery maturity, operational technical support, and observability workflows comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The audit examines change control discipline, configuration management database (CMDB) accuracy, incident resolution efficacy, and proactive operational event correlation.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T8: This chapter examines the fiduciary model, technological financial transparency, and strategic technology governance comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation analyzes infrastructure cost predictability and showback across business units, software licensing optimization, and technological investment alignment with organizational priorities.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T9: This chapter addresses the diagnosis of the digital workplace, collaboration solutions, and user endpoint fleets comprising {tower_title} across {client_name}. The analysis evaluates device fleet standardization and homogeneity, automated lifecycle staging and patching, digital employee experience (DEX), and secure endpoint access across distributed workspaces.
ch3_intro_by_tower.T10: This chapter analyzes dedicated operational platforms, activity execution systems, and field peripherals underpinning {tower_title} across {client_name}. The evaluation audits hardware resilience at critical operating points, transactional continuity during network contingencies, and the modernization posture of core operational systems.

ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T1: Scoring a technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), datacenter facilities across {client_name} sit at the threshold of Level 3. Solid electromechanical power and fire suppression defenses ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrast with thermal fragility in processing rooms ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where uncontained thermal zones and uneven cooling distribution introduce localized operational risk.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T2: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), compute infrastructure operates at its physical limits across {client_name}. Baseline hypervisor stability ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with compute resource saturation ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), eliminating the resilience buffer required to absorb host failure without disrupting core business transactions.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T3: Network infrastructure achieves a technical score of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}). Campus switching resilience across primary sites ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with the gap in automation and observability ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where manual configuration workflows and telemetry blindspots impede agile fault isolation across remote locations.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T4: Rated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), corporate storage demonstrates dependable snapshot replication ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0). The critical challenge lies within storage tiering architecture ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where the absence of immutable ransomware vaults and restrictive disk provisioning force technical staff at {client_name} into continuous manual quota containment.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T5: Scoring {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), operational resilience exhibits a critical gap against enterprise recovery tolerances across {client_name}. Operational backup reliability ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with continuous recovery fragility ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where insufficient geographic independence between redundant systems leaves services vulnerable to systemic regional disruption.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T6: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), cybersecurity governance operates under structured operational controls across {client_name}. While perimeter and telemetry defenses demonstrate verified maturity ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0), continuous privileged access governance and secrets automation ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0) remain critical priorities to sustain regulatory compliance.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T7: Scoring a technical maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), IT service management operates reactively across {client_name}. System monitoring visibility ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with the absence of formal problem management ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), consuming critical engineering capacity in recurring incident troubleshooting.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T8: Technology governance achieves a score of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}). Disciplined procurement control across {client_name} ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) coexists with cost allocation opacity ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where uncoordinated cloud commitments and software licensing constraints restrict compute scalability.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T9: With a consolidated maturity of {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), the digital workplace exhibits structured hardware fleet management ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0). The primary friction lies within workplace operations and support ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where unstandardized workstation configurations and manual provisioning introduce operational overhead across {client_name}.
ch3_scorecard_by_tower.T10: Evaluated at {score_val} out of 5.0 ({maturity_tier_label}), core transactional processing platforms represent a critical operational dependency across {client_name}. Established transaction processing stability ({strongest_pillar_name}, {strongest_pillar_score}/5.0) contrasts with legacy interface rigidity ({weakest_pillar_name}, {weakest_pillar_score}/5.0), where monolithic batch architectures and tightly coupled integrations constrain operational agility.

AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.methodology_intro: {domain_name} の数理的露出は Open FAIR™ 可用性・サービス停止レセプターを介してモデル化され、計画外のサービス停止による財務的影響を捉えます。

AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.vector_alpha_label: 直接的な取引損失およびSLA違反損失
AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.vector_alpha_desc: 重要資産におけるサービス利用不可による財務的影響。
AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.vector_beta_label: 緊急対策室および復旧エンジニアリング労力
AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.vector_beta_desc: 状態復元および根本原因解決に必要な計画外のエンジニアリング労力。
AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.vector_gamma_label: 二次的な顧客離れとブランド価値の低下
AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.vector_gamma_desc: 長期化するシステム不安定性に起因する二次的な商業的損失。
AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.prioritization_rationale: 改善順序は、MTTRの削減と影響範囲の封じ込めに厳密に従います。
AVAILABILITY_OUTAGE.section_title: 4.1. サービス停止およびダウンタイム損失推定モデル

PRODUCTIVITY_TOIL.vector_gamma_desc: 手動でのサポート対応や繰り返しの運用作業で消費される人的資本。
PRODUCTIVITY_TOIL.prioritization_rationale: 改善順序は、ワークフロー自動化と摩擦の排除を最優先します。

annex_ch4_context_gamma.cloud_native: クラウドネイティブFinOpsトポロジ（γ={gamma:.2f}）: インフラの財務エクスポージャーは、オンデマンドコンピュートの肥大化、最適化されていないリザーブドインスタンス、マルチリージョンの孤立リソースに起因します。
annex_ch4_context_gamma.on_prem: オンプレミスインフラおよびコアライセンス統治（γ={gamma:.2f}）: 資本の非効率性は、遊休ハイパーコンバージド容量、コアベースの仮想化ライセンス追加精算負債、ハードウェア減価償却の摩擦に集中しています。
annex_ch4_context_gamma.hybrid: ハイブリッドクラウドアビトラージおよびエッジサイジング（γ={gamma:.2f}）: 財務摩擦は、ワークロード配置の非対称性、オンプレミスとクラウドの二重運用コスト、調整されていないマルチベンダー契約から生じます。

annex_ch4_context_beta.clinical: 急性の臨床的脆弱性（β={beta:.2f}）: リアルタイムの患者生体情報および集中治療室（ICU）監視はバッファ許容度がほぼゼロであり、システム停止は即座に診療・トリアージの遅延に直結します。
annex_ch4_context_beta.synchronous: 同期決済の即時感応度（β={beta:.2f}）: 決済レールおよびコア台帳トランザクションは停止バッファを持たず、即時の決済不能ペナルティおよび流動性SLA違反を引き起こします。
annex_ch4_context_beta.high_tempo: 高頻度オペレーショナルエクスポージャー（β={beta:.2f}）: 業務オペレーションの即時中断および直接的な収益損失を防ぐため、継続的なサービス可用性が極めて重要です。
annex_ch4_context_beta.buffered_silo: 物理的サイロおよび在庫バッファ（β={beta:.2f}）: プラントの出荷および製造は中間在庫バッファや振替シフトによって部分的に保護され、短期の障害における直線的な収益損失を防ぎます。

de.gloss_mcda_crit_extrema: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Extreme]:** Assesses the level of direct dependency that key operational processes have on this domain. Core business operations depend critically on this platform, and an outage would cause immediate disruption of essential services.
de.gloss_mcda_crit_alta: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - High]:** Reflects high operational dependency, though a brief latency tolerance exists before core business continuity is disrupted.
de.gloss_mcda_crit_media: **Business Criticality (MCDA) [{val}% - Medium]:** The domain provides supportive or back-office services whose temporary downtime is manageable via standard contingency procedures.
de.gloss_mcda_reg_critica: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Critical]:** Severe regulatory exposure under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001), where security deficiencies directly incur high statutory penalties and direct corporate liability.
de.gloss_mcda_reg_moderada: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Moderate]:** Strict corporate compliance and security baseline mandates apply, requiring periodic independent IT control audits.
de.gloss_mcda_reg_estandar: **Regulatory Pressure (MCDA) [{val}% - Standard]:** Standard operational compliance based on engineering best practices without direct statutory critical scrutiny.
de.gloss_mcda_viab_fav: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Feasible]:** Transformation feasibility is favorable. Modernization initiatives can be delivered with mature technologies and market resources without critical disruption.
de.gloss_mcda_viab_comp: **Operational Feasibility (MCDA) [{val}% - Complex]:** High execution complexity due to structural technical debt, maintenance bottlenecks, or specialized skill scarcity.
de.gloss_dii_alta: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Stability]:** The extremely low Decision Instability Index mathematically certifies that findings are robust and unaffected by small evidence variations.
de.gloss_dii_mod: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - Moderate Stability]:** Moderate sensitivity; findings are substantially stable though specific sub-scores depend on evolving architectural interpretation.
de.gloss_dii_vol: **Diagnostic Consistency (DII) [{val}% - High Sensitivity]:** High volatility; limited evidentiary backing suggests further confirmation is required to lock target maturity scores.
de.gloss_erc_alta: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - High]:** High structural influence; a critical outage in this domain easily propagates cascades destabilizing connected enterprise systems.
de.gloss_erc_media: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Medium]:** Moderate structural influence; disruption remains contained, impacting only immediately adjacent workloads.
de.gloss_erc_baja: **Cascading Fault Propagation (ERC) [{val} - Low/Isolated]:** Low structural influence; failures remain strictly isolated within this technical perimeter without holding-wide impact.
de.gloss_spof_crit: **Single Point of Failure (SPOF) [YES - Critical]:** This domain represents an unmitigated structural bottleneck without sufficient failover, requiring immediate remediation.
de.gloss_spof_stable: **Single Point of Failure (SPOF) [NO - Stable]:** This domain does not act as an isolated single point of failure within the overall operational topology.

de.systemic_resilience_intro: Um die plattformübergreifende Resilienz zu messen, berechnet die Engine fortschrittliche Entscheidungsindikatoren unter Verwendung multikriterieller Entscheidungsmodelle und Netzwerkausbreitungsalgorithmen:
systemic_resilience_indicators_list: 1. **Geschäftskritikalität (MCDA) [Bereich 0% bis 100%]:** Werte über 80% (Extrem - Kritische Säule) zeigen, dass die Domäne direkt wesentliche Kerngeschäftsprozesse stützt.
2. **Regulatorischer Druck (MCDA) [Bereich 0% bis 100%]:** Werte über 80% (Kritisch) weisen auf strenge gesetzliche Auflagen (z. B. NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001) hin.
3. **Operative Machbarkeit (MCDA) [Bereich 0% bis 100%]:** Misst die technische und organisatorische Umsetzbarkeit geplanter Initiativen.
4. **Diagnostischer Instabilitätsindex (DII) [Bereich 0% bis 100%]:** Quantifiziert die mathematische Stabilität und Sensitivität der Bewertung gegenüber Datenschwankungen.
5. **Kaskadenfehler-Ausbreitungsindex (ERC) [Bereich 0,000 bis 1,000]:** Verwendet PageRank-Netzwerkzentralität zur Messung der Ausbreitungsfähigkeit technischer Störungen.
6. **Single Point of Failure (SPOF) [JA / NEIN]:** Strukturelle Redundanzklassifikation. 'JA' signalisiert fehlende aktive Redundanz bei geschäftskritischen Komponenten.

de.appendix_fair_rationale_p: Traditionelle qualitative Risikomatrizen bieten eine erste Übersicht, lassen jedoch die versicherungsmathematische Präzision vermissen, die für Budgetentscheidungen und den ROI-Nachweis erforderlich ist. Dieses Gutachten wendet daher den Standard Open FAIR™ (ISO/IEC 27005) an.
de.appendix_fair_dual_layer_p: Um nachzuvollziehen, wie sich technische Mängel auf die Unternehmensbilanz auswirken, rekonstruiert das Modell die Schadensfälle Schritt für Schritt ('Die Biografie eines Vorfalls') in zwei Schichten:
de.appendix_fair_dual_layer_b1: Schicht 1: Schwachstellenmodellierung (FAIR-CAM™) - Stochastische Kalibrierung der Kontrollwirksamkeit: Kalibriert die Wahrscheinlichkeit (_VULN_), dass Bedrohungen Schutzmaßnahmen überwinden, anhand der auditierten Reife. Primärschäden werden über Lognormalverteilungen modelliert.
de.appendix_fair_dual_layer_b2: Schicht 2: Sekundäre Exposition und Sorgfaltspflicht (FAIR-MAM™) - Bedingte Ausbreitung regulatorischer Risiken: Simuliert katastrophale Sekundärverluste (Bußgelder unter {reg_name} bis zu {reg_fine_limit}) anhand kontinuierlicher logistischer Übergangskurven.
de.appendix_fair_sim_kernel_p: Der Kern dieses Gutachtens liegt in seiner mathematischen Architektur: eine **Monte-Carlo-Simulation mit 10.000 Durchläufen**, gesteuert durch einen zweistufigen kollektiven Risikoprozess nach Basler Standards (Basel III):
appendix_fair_sim_bullets: Experten-Elicitation (Adversarialer Multi-Agenten-Konsens): Bayessche Kalibrierung zur Vermeidung von Doppelzählungen.
Bedrohungshäufigkeit (Negative Binomialverteilung): Modelliert Häufungseffekte und Überdispersion von Angriffen.
Kontrollwirksamkeit (Binomialprozess): Simuliert das Abwehren oder Versagen von Schutzmaßnahmen.
Schadensschwere (Lognormalverteilung mit Soft-Truncation): Modelliert Tail-Risiken unter Berücksichtigung gesetzlicher Höchstgrenzen.
Multivariate Korrelation (Gauß-Copula): Verknüpft Primärschäden direkt mit sekundären Sanktionen.
de.appendix_fair_metrics_intro: Aus den 10.000 Simulationsdurchläufen leitet die Engine die kumulative Verlustverteilung und drei zentrale Kennzahlen für Managemententscheidungen ab:
appendix_fair_metrics_bullets: Annual Loss Exposure (ALE): Der arithmetische Mittelwert aller Schadensszenarien als Basiskennzahl der Kosten des Nichthandelns.
Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR / Expected Shortfall): Der Erwartungswert der schwersten 2,5% aller Extremverluste (Tail Risk).
Plausibler Schadensbereich (P10 - P90): Das operative Schwankungsintervall für eine realistische Budget- und Investitionsplanung.
de.appendix_c_custody_p1: Um Unveränderlichkeit und forensische Nachvollziehbarkeit für kritische Infrastruktur-Audits zu gewährleisten, dokumentiert diese Übersicht die Primärquellen der Untersuchung:
de.matrix_dim_1_path_a:
• Annualized cost of inaction estimated at **{currency}{formatted_ale_item}**/year (ALE from operational friction and unplanned downtime).
• Latent exposure in a severe crisis or cascading outage scenario reaching up to **{currency}{formatted_p90}** (P90).
• Cumulative technical debt growth and continuous rise in maintenance overhead over a 3- to 5-year horizon.
de.matrix_dim_1_path_b:
• Progressive amortization of structural technical debt through targeted investment.
• Over **80%** reduction in systemic risk exposure and elimination of single points of failure.
• Defensible ROI grounded in eliminated downtime and reduced manual toil.
de.matrix_dim_2_path_a:
• Reactive siloed operations heavily dependent on manual firefighting.
• Escalating Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) and reliance on emergency triage.
• Late incident detection reported by end users or business operations.
de.matrix_dim_2_path_b:
• Unified real-time telemetry with proactive incident prevention prior to service impact.
• Radical MTTR reduction through automated procedures and executable runbooks.
• Service Level Agreements (SLAs) guaranteed by continuous observability.
de.matrix_dim_3_path_a:
• Structural difficulty demonstrating continuous compliance during internal and external audits.
• Exposure to non-compliance findings and operational contingencies under applicable frameworks (e.g. NIS2, ISO 27001, ISO 22301).
de.matrix_dim_3_path_b:
• Auditable compliance by design through structured technical governance.
• Minimized non-compliance exposure and automated documentation traceability.
de.matrix_dim_4_path_a:
• Continuous cognitive overload on IT specialists handling low-value manual toil.
• Engineering fatigue, risk of critical operational knowledge loss, and delayed strategic projects.
de.matrix_dim_4_path_b:
• Standardization and automation of repetitive tasks, liberating engineering capacity.
• Refocusing technical talent on innovation, business scalability, and strategic growth.
de.appendix_fair_convergence_note: *(Hinweis zu Konvergenz und Bruttorisiko: 10.000 Iterationen garantieren mathematische Konvergenz unter dem Zentralen Grenzwertsatz. Beträge stellen das latente Bruttorisiko vor Risikotransfermaßnahmen dar und dienen der Priorisierung technischer Investitionen).*

methodology_three_phases_bullets: **Phase 1: Evidence Ingestion & Operational Verification:** On-site technical inspection, engineering interviews, and network/facility topology validation.
**Phase 2: Topological Dependency Modeling & SPOF Analysis:** Cascading failure propagation analysis mapping facility disruptions to core organizational operations.
**Phase 3: Quantitative Actuarial Simulation (Open FAIR):** 10,000-run Monte Carlo stochastic modeling quantifying annualized financial loss exposure (ALE) and P90 tail risk.
de.cross_cutting_debt_title: Cross-Cutting Technical Debt Analysis & Structural Risk Patterns
de.cross_cutting_debt_intro: Beyond vertical pillar baselines, the assessment identifies three horizontal friction patterns spanning the entire infrastructure:
de.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_1: **1. Mangel an kontinuierlicher Telemetrie und nicht überwachte elektrische Kapazität:** Das Management der elektrischen und thermischen Kapazität verfügt über keine digitale Echtzeittelemetrie an Hauptverteilern und Rack-PDUs.
de.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_2: **2. Operational Silos Between Facilities (BMS) and Central Enterprise IT Observability:** Electromechanical infrastructure operates decoupled from corporate monitoring. Environmental anomalies fail to trigger correlated early warnings, causing degradations to be discovered only after server cluster outages.
de.cross_cutting_debt_pattern_3: **3. Unstrukturierte Wartungsverfahren und Arbeitserlaubnislücken (ePtW):** Vorbeugende Wartungsrundgänge, Umschaltprüfungen und Zutrittskontrollen für externe Dienstleister verfügen über keine formellen digitalen Autorisierungsworkflows.
de.rore_value_hexagon_title: The Return on Resilience & Efficiency Hexagon (RoRE / TBM & FinOps)
de.rore_value_hexagon_intro: Infrastructure risk mitigation unlocks direct economic value structured across six strategic levers under the TBM and FinOps frameworks:
rore_value_hexagon_bullets: **1. Labor Capital Recovery (Lean IT):** Eliminating reactive manual rounds and physical clamp measurements, freeing engineering capacity for core innovation initiatives.
**2. Cost of Delay Reduction:** Accelerating capacity provisioning and facilitating seamless post-merger technology onboarding for organizational acquisitions (M&A).

**3. Capacity Optimization & Operational Efficiency:** Eliminating throughput bottlenecks, over-provisioning, and resource waste, reducing operational platform overhead and infrastructure energy consumption by up to 28%.
**4. Extended Support Cost Avoidance:** Phasing out end-of-life (EoL) infrastructure before facing punitive non-warranty vendor maintenance pricing tiers.
**5. Tail-Risk Balance Sheet Mitigation (CVaR):** Insulating operational cash flows against catastrophic multi-day outages threatening commercial revenue and continuous operations.

**6. Regulatory & Governance Compliance Assurance:** Continuous audit-grade telemetry and incident records ensuring alignment with international resilience frameworks and preventing punitive regulatory sanctions.

ch3_intro_archetypes.INFRASTRUCTURE_PHYSICAL: This chapter presents the technical assessment of physical facilities, electromechanical power distribution, and plant networking across {tower_name} at {client_name}. The analysis evaluates infrastructure resilience across three dimensions: power and precision cooling redundancy, single point of failure (SPOF) elimination, and preventive maintenance discipline.
ch3_intro_archetypes.COMPUTE_PLATFORMS: This chapter documents the technical diagnostic of compute platforms, virtualization clusters, and workload execution environments comprising {tower_name} at {client_name}. The assessment examines cluster capacity to sustain continuous transaction throughput, hypervisor memory saturation, and operating system support lifecycles.
ch3_intro_archetypes.SECURITY_GOVERNANCE: This section presents the technical evaluation of persistence mechanisms, access controls, and operational governance across {tower_name} at {client_name}. The analysis verifies data immutability, infrastructure defense resilience, and contingency recovery readiness safeguarding enterprise continuity.

de.ch3_intro_p1: This chapter executes the technical diagnostic of the technology platform at {client_name}, evaluating the {tower_name} infrastructure across three analytical dimensions: (1) architectural resilience against single points of failure (SPOFs) and redundancy deficits; (2) physical and logical obsolescence relative to vendor support lifecycles; and (3) the maturity of operational runbooks and preventive maintenance regimes. Triangulating these factors under the CMMI framework establishes the operational risk baseline and substantiates modernization priorities.

de.ch4_methodological_intro: This technical diagnostic applies The Open Group international O-FAIR (Factor Analysis of Information Risk) standard to model, quantify, and prioritize infrastructure risk exposure in real financial terms. To avoid the "Flaw of Averages" (where fixed single-point estimates distort true risk), the platform engine executes a 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo actuarial simulation algorithm for every detected finding.

ch4_sec1_domain_context.INFRASTRUCTURE_PHYSICAL: Within {tower_name}, an unplanned electrical or cooling failure directly halts server rooms and network gear at primary facilities of {client_name}. This disrupts critical operational support services and transactional business platforms, resulting in an operational stoppage rate of {hourly_rate_est}.
ch4_sec1_domain_context.COMPUTE_PLATFORMS: Within {tower_name}, a critical compute cluster outage or hypervisor lock simultaneously interrupts transactional database instances, enterprise ERP, and operational management systems. This halts customer orders, billing dispatches, and workflow coordination at an operational cost of {hourly_rate_est}.
ch4_sec1_domain_context.SECURITY_GOVERNANCE: Within {tower_name}, a critical security compromise or privileged identity lockout disrupts core authentication and transactional pipelines, forcing operational suspension to verify authorization integrity at an estimated rate of {hourly_rate_est}.

de.components_evaluated_lead: The technical scope evaluated within this tower encompasses the following key components and subsystems:
de.default_primary_workloads: mission-critical customer-facing workloads, real-time transaction pipelines, and core enterprise digital services
de.exec_narrative_p1: Every technological architecture upholds a financial promise. For {tower_name}, that promise currently rests on fragile foundations (Level {score_display} - {global_band}). Our forensic analysis reveals that the underlying infrastructure is not suffering from a lack of capacity, but rather from a silent erosion of operational resilience: structural vulnerabilities where an unpredicted fault holds the potential to sever {client_name}'s business continuity.
de.exec_narrative_p2: To translate this technical fragility into boardroom economics, we rejected arbitrary industry averages. By applying an actuarial model calibrated against actual exposed corporate turnover ({effective_exposed_revenue_formatted} {currency_code}), we established a composite downtime burn rate of **{hourly_cost}/h** (incorporating a {sector_impact_factor_pct}% direct revenue velocity penalty, SLA breach accruals, and incident labor burden). This valuation directly links the platform's vulnerabilities with {client_name}'s operating cash flow.
de.exec_narrative_p3: Furthermore, to prevent mathematical inflation, we deduplicated overlapping blast radii via joint failure probability: true net exposure stands at **{ale_hours} critical hours annually**, crystallizing a net Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE) of **{ale_formatted}**. Under a severe tail-risk scenario (90th percentile), an uncontrollable outage could cripple operations for up to {p90_hours} hours, incurring a catastrophic exposure of **{p90_formatted}**.
de.exec_narrative_p4: Deferring remediation is not cost containment; it is the unhedged underwriting of an operational catastrophe. Executing the proposed target roadmap eliminates the current operational paralysis and automates resilience in {tower_name}. This capital allocation converts an unpredictable technical liability into hardened operational equity, safeguarding both {client_name}'s EBITDA and institutional trust against severe disruption.

de.p90_callout_body_template: Consistent with the Chapter 1 executive synthesis, actuarial modeling at the 90th percentile (P90) evaluates a compound failure triggered by {compound_failure_trigger}. Under this asymptotic stress regime, the physical reconstruction, state synchronization, and operational verification window extends up to {p90_recovery_hours} hours. The projected maximum contingent financial exposure reaches {p90_total_contingency}, comprising {direct_stoppage_loss} in direct operational stoppage losses and {secondary_disaster_spend} in secondary disaster expenditures (emergency OEM vendor escalation, expedited hardware logistics, and Tier-3 specialized triage).
de.p90_callout_p1: To evaluate the practical resilience limit of this capability tower, the model simulates a severe, plausible scenario in which multiple critical failures occur simultaneously ({compound_failure_trigger}). Unlike routine isolated incidents, this case examines the operational reality when both primary systems and their backup mechanisms fail concurrently.
de.p90_callout_p2: In a disruption of this magnitude, recovery requires more than restarting equipment; teams must rebuild operations step by step and verify that no critical business data has been corrupted. Under current technical conditions, fully restoring service and validating data consistency would require up to {p90_recovery_hours} hours.
de.p90_callout_p3: The total financial exposure of this scenario reaches {p90_total_contingency}. This impact breaks down clearly into two categories: {direct_stoppage_loss} in direct losses from halted commercial and operational activity during the outage, and {secondary_disaster_spend} in extraordinary emergency expenses (such as urgent third-party specialist intervention, priority vendor support, and expedited operational recovery services).

de.sec4_1_alpha_reconciliation: Downtime Cost Scaling by Failure Scope: The baseline corporate rate ({base_rate}/h) represents a complete shutdown of all business operations. Because most technical incidents do not halt 100% of the company, the model scales the hourly cost according to the actual scope of each failure: 70% ({rate_70}/h) for core critical platforms, 40% ({rate_40}/h) for intermediate systems with partial degradation, and 20% ({rate_20}/h) for isolated peripheral components. This ensures each risk card realistically reflects the financial impact of its specific domain.
de.sle_derivation_formula_bullet: • **Exact Financial Derivation (SLE):** {effective_hours}h operational disruption at {hourly_rate}/hr ({alpha_pct}% operational impact factor over baseline downtime cost of {base_rate}/hr) = {sle_formatted}.

de.tomo_ch1_headline: Evaluation of Current Infrastructure and Operations at {client_name}
de.tomo_ch1_lead_in: The transversal audit highlights four critical risk factors requiring immediate leadership action:
de.tomo_ch1_p1: Die umfassende Bewertung des Technologieportfolios von {client} erstreckt sich über {domain_count} operative Domänen und ergibt einen globalen Reifegradindex von {score} von 5.00 ({cmmi_label}). Dieses Profil zeigt eine Architektur mit gefestigten operativen Fähigkeiten in ihren führenden Assets, die jedoch strukturellen Asymmetrien und konzentrierten finanziellen Risiken ausgesetzt ist, welche eine prioritäre Executive Governance erfordern.
de.tomo_ch1_p3:
Die quantitative versicherungsmathematische Risikobewertung nach dem internationalen Open FAIR™-Standard (Factor Analysis of Information Risk) etabliert drei komplementäre Dimensionen für die Entscheidungsfindung der Geschäftsführung:

1. **Jährlicher Erwartungsschaden (ALE) von {formatted_ale} annualisiert:** Spiegelt den erwarteten durchschnittlichen Verlust in einem regulären Geschäftsjahr wider, bestehend aus laufenden betrieblichen Reibungsverlusten, ungeplanten Support-Überstunden und Wartungsineffizienzen.

2. **Einzelausfall durch Schweren Störfall von bis zu {worst_incident_cost}:** Entspricht dem direkten Betriebsstillstand im am stärksten exponierten Bereich ({worst_incident_code} - {worst_incident_domain}) bei einem isolierten Plattformausfall.

3. **Kumuliertes Jährliches Krisenszenario von {formatted_p90}:** Modelliert die aggregierte finanzielle Belastung, falls in einem schwierigen Geschäftsjahr mehrere schwere Vorfälle über verschiedene Plattformen hinweg zusammentreffen.

Diese Dimensionierung versetzt die Führungsebene in die Lage, Modernisierungsinvestitionen gezielt dort zu steuern, wo der höchste Risikominderungseffekt pro investierter Kapitaleinheit erzielt wird.
de.tomo_ch2_footnote: *Methodological note: The consolidated index of {global_score} out of 5.00 reflects the weighted average by operational criticality across domains (the simple arithmetic mean is {simple_mean}).*
de.tomo_ch2_intro: Die Bewertung des technologischen Reifegrads bestimmt die tatsächliche Fähigkeit der aktuellen Architektur, die Betriebskontinuität aufrechtzuerhalten, industrielle Prozesse zu skalieren und Unterbrechungsrisiken zu mindern. Das Analysemodell prüft die 10 Technologietürme nach der CMMI-Standardskala (Capability Maturity Model Integration) von 1,00 bis 5,00 und stützt sich dabei ausschließlich auf empirische Nachweise aus der Infrastruktur, den Anwendungen und den Betriebsprozessen der Organisation.
de.tomo_ch2_summary: The CMMI diagnostic places {client_name} at a consolidated index of {global_score} out of 5.00 ({maturity_tier_label}), reflecting an operational foundation with established baseline capabilities alongside inter-domain disparities. Technology domains with the largest deficits against sector benchmarks require targeted modernization roadmaps to mitigate technical debt.
de.tomo_ch3_financial_hierarchy_body:
To ensure complete transparency for the CFO and Executive Board, the model defines three complementary financial metrics:
1. **Expected Annual Loss Exposure (ALE P50):** Modeled annual operational loss exposure across all evaluated technology domains in the current state.
2. **Single Major Outage Impact (P90 Local):** Maximum loss under an unredundant technical outage halting operations across primary facilities during {duration_str} of downtime and transactional verification.
3. **Annual Aggregate Severe Portfolio Risk (P90 Annual):** The 90th percentile aggregate portfolio loss under compounding adverse operational events across all operating units.
de.tomo_ch3_financial_hierarchy_title: Actuarial Reconciliation Framework & Metric Hierarchy (Open FAIR™)
de.tomo_ch3_intro: To eliminate the ambiguity of subjective RAG matrices, this assessment executes the Open FAIR™ standard driven by 10,000-run Monte Carlo stochastic engines, independently evaluating Loss Event Frequency (LEF / TEF) and Loss Magnitude (SLE / LM) across structural failure vectors.
de.tomo_ch3_p90_1: Während die in Abschnitt 3.3 detaillierten Risikokarten schwere Einzelereignisse bewerten, simuliert das stochastische Monte-Carlo-Modell das jährliche Gesamtschadensrisiko des Technologieportfolios.
de.tomo_ch3_p90_2: Under an unfavorable operational year where multiple moderate and severe incidents materialize concurrently across the ten technology domains during the same budget cycle, annual aggregate portfolio losses reach {formatted_p90} at the 90th percentile (Annual P90).
de.tomo_ch3_p90_3: This {formatted_p90} figure establishes the unprovisioned annual exposure ceiling that fully justifies the strategic technical standardization and contingency investments detailed in the target roadmap.
de.tomo_ch3_rate: The composite hourly downtime baseline is calibrated at **{baseline_rate}**, reconciling operational loss of velocity, contractual SLA penalties, and emergency recovery burden. At operational facilities and primary delivery sites, the local hourly rate reflects the direct interruption of business transaction throughput.
de.tomo_ch3_tier1_desc: Disruption of core transaction processing, compute capacity saturation, and corporate licensing lifecycle.
de.tomo_ch3_tier2_desc: Absence of environmental IoT telemetry, manual change management, and multi-vendor contract duplication.
de.tomo_ch3_tier3_desc: Non-standardized patch updates and lack of self-service catalog.

de.tomo_ch4_t10_text: Local infrastructure and support operations sustain daily field workflows across distributed sites, offering opportunities to standardize edge telemetry and lifecycle management.
de.tomo_ch4_t1_text: Primary technical facilities provide continuous operational support for enterprise compute and connectivity workloads. Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems and diesel backup generators maintain regular preventive maintenance, operating within conventional thermal profiles that require continuous environmental telemetry.
de.tomo_ch4_t2_text: Core compute environments rely on virtualized platforms experiencing high memory utilization, constraining automated failover headroom during physical node maintenance windows. The platform requires a structured modernization roadmap to align hypervisor licensing with organizational growth.
de.tomo_ch4_t3_text: The enterprise network fabric interconnects corporate headquarters, regional offices, and operational sites. Core inter-site communications leverage dedicated redundant connectivity, while distributed facilities utilize managed WAN links over secure tunnels, representing a strategic opportunity for SD-WAN convergence.
de.tomo_ch4_t4_text: Core enterprise storage relies on Almacenamiento Centralizado FAS/AFF arrays via NFS and Fibre Channel. While operational maturity is high (CMMI Level 3), missing WORM SnapLock immutability leaves backup repositories exposed to ransomware encryption. Controller multipathing requires validation to prevent I/O bottlenecks during firmware updates.
de.tomo_ch4_t5_text: Business continuity and disaster recovery procedures maintain secondary replications of critical data repositories, with full operational resilience requiring automated switchover testing to minimize recovery time objectives (RTO).
de.tomo_ch4_t6_text: Perimeter security enforces firewall filtering across major ingress points. Identity governance requires federating disparate directory forests into a unified model, deploying Privileged Access Management (PAM) for administrative accounts, and deepening network segmentation.
de.tomo_ch4_t7_text: Transactional core runs on Oracle Database and SQL Server engines with concentrated administration knowledge. The ITSM platform lacks an automated CMDB federated with the infrastructure digital twin.
de.tomo_ch4_t8_text: Core ERP platforms and business application suites constitute the operational heart of the enterprise. Cloud workloads and SaaS software subscriptions require unified cost-allocation tagging to optimize recurring spend and eliminate licensing overlap.
de.tomo_ch4_t8_title: 4.8. Enterprise Applications and Cloud Cost Governance (T8)
de.tomo_ch4_t9_text: Digital workplace platforms provide standardized productivity and collaboration suites across cloud endpoints, requiring unified mobile device management policies across all distributed offices.

tomo_nexus_catalog.mechanism: Hypervisors and management consoles rely on the general enterprise directory without Tier-0 privileged account isolation.
tomo_nexus_catalog.impact: A security incident on standard user accounts can laterally propagate to core virtualization management.

tomo_nexus_catalog.mechanism: Open airflow distribution without contained hot/cold aisles creates hotspots in high-density compute racks.
tomo_nexus_catalog.impact: Thermal degradation of physical hardware components can trigger unplanned host shutdowns.

tomo_nexus_catalog.mechanism: Secondary backup repositories reside on the same storage fabric as primary production volumes without air-gap.
tomo_nexus_catalog.impact: A catastrophic storage control-plane fault or ransomware sweep threatens backup availability.

tomo_nexus_catalog.mechanism: Core transactional terminals validate settlement records against central enterprise systems across single-homed network tunnels.
tomo_nexus_catalog.impact: A transient local network disruption immediately halts physical truck dispatching at the affected facility.
